desc_en: Slams down hard with a lightning flash
prompt_en: The screen first flashes brightly twice and a lightning bolt appears; the text slams down instantly from 2x size and shrinks back to its original size, trembling slightly on landing, then keeps a soft outer glow. The whole sequence lasts about 2.4 seconds, with a fast, explosive rhythm.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: A laser slices the text in two
prompt_en: A glowing laser line cuts rapidly from left to right across the middle of the text; after it passes, the top half of the text shifts up-left and the bottom half shifts down-right, tilting slightly, pauses for a moment, then comes back together. About 2.6 seconds per cycle, with a crisp sci-fi feel.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: Text flips and bounces like a coin
prompt_en: Each character flips two full turns around the Y axis like a coin and jumps upward, then bounces once more, small, when it lands, with a sequential delay of about 0.14 seconds between characters. About 2.4 seconds per cycle, light and playful.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Text explodes and flies in all directions
prompt_en: The text first swells slightly to build up energy, then each character explodes randomly in a different direction, spinning, shrinking and fading out; after a pause, the characters fly back into place to form the text again, alternating between the primary color and an accent color. About 2.8 seconds per cycle, with a strong sense of impact.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: Text dissolves into particles
prompt_en: From left to right, each character blurs in turn, drifts up and to the right, and fades out, while many small square particles appear around it and float away; after disappearing, the text re-emerges. About 3 seconds per cycle, dramatic.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: Zooms with a heartbeat and spreads ripples
prompt_en: The text zooms in twice in a row like a heartbeat — “thump-thump” — then returns to its original size; with each beat, two circular ripples spread out from the center at the same time and fade away. About 1.3 seconds per beat.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: Text rotates in a kaleidoscope
prompt_en: The same word is copied 12 times, arranged radially around a center point in the shape of a flower; the whole group keeps rotating slowly while each copy stretches outward and breathes back in at the same time, forming a kaleidoscope effect, with adjacent copies alternating between light and dark tones. One full rotation takes about 7 seconds.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: Countdown numbers slam down hard
prompt_en: The countdown “3, 2, 1, GO!” appears in sequence; each number slams down forcefully from 3x size and rebounds to its original size, about 0.75 seconds per number, with GO! highlighted in an accent color. Bold black type, with a strong opening feel.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: Text undulates like a wave
prompt_en: Each character rises and falls in sequence and sways slightly from side to side, forming a continuously flowing wave, with the characters alternating between two tones. About 1.4 seconds per wave, with a relaxed, joyful summer feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Shakes frame by frame, like stop-motion animation
prompt_en: Each character trembles and rotates slightly at random in a discontinuous, frame-by-frame jumping manner (like stop-motion animation, with no smooth transitions), with each character offset in rhythm from the others. About a 0.9-second loop, with a handmade toy feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Text falls like rain
prompt_en: The entire block's background is covered with vertical columns of kana text falling continuously from top to bottom like rain, each column at a different speed (about 3–5 seconds to fall), a few columns in an accent color and the rest in low-contrast tones, for a fantastical background feel.
style_en: Flowing Background
txt_en: あいうえおかきくけこさしすせそたちつてとなにぬねのはひふへほまみむめもやゆよらりるれろ

desc_en: Magnifies text with a magnifying glass
prompt_en: A circular magnifying glass moves back and forth, left and right, across the text; the text inside the lens is enlarged about 1.5x and switches to an accent color, while the text outside the lens is fainter; the magnifying glass has a handle. About 6 seconds per round trip, with an explanatory / discovery feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: Decodes from gibberish into real text
prompt_en: The text starts as constantly jumping gibberish (katakana, symbols and numbers), then decodes from left to right, character by character, into the correct text and switches to an accent color, pauses, then starts over. A pixel dot-matrix font, with a hacker sci-fi feel.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: Text topples like dominoes
prompt_en: Each character pivots on its bottom-right corner and topples to the right in sequence by about 72 degrees, falling in a chain like dominoes, then all stand back up together after a pause. There is a floor line beneath the text. About 3.2 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: A gradient flows through the text
prompt_en: The text is filled with a multi-color gradient that keeps flowing from left to right inside the letters. Large bold type, about 3 seconds per flow cycle, with a fashionable headline feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: Rings of text rotate in opposite directions
prompt_en: Two rings of circularly arranged text: the outer ring rotates slowly clockwise and the inner ring rotates faster counterclockwise, with the inner and outer rings distinguished by different tones. The outer ring takes about 9 seconds per revolution and the inner ring about 6 seconds, with a hypnotic logo feel.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: A reflection swaying on the water's surface
prompt_en: Below the text is a thin horizontal line; beneath the line is an upside-down reflection that is semi-transparent and fades out as it goes down, continually tilting and swaying side to side like ripples on water, while the text above also floats slightly. A calm night-scene feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: Text bounces letter by letter
prompt_en: Each character in sequence squashes flat, springs up, lands and squashes and rebounds again, with the squash-and-stretch elasticity of a small ball, only one character jumping at a time. About 2.2 seconds per cycle, with a cute MV feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion Canva Style Canva Bounce Bounce

desc_en: Text flutters like a flag
prompt_en: There is a flagpole at the left side of the text; each character flips in 3D and tilts in sequence, forming a wave like a flag fluttering in the wind. About 1.3 seconds per wave, with a powerful cheering feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Gravity reverses and it bounces upward
prompt_en: Each character first accelerates as it “falls” upward to the top and flips upside down, pauses, then drops back into place and flips upright, with a small bounce on landing, the characters staggered in sequence from each other. About 3 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Text is pulled in as if by a magnet
prompt_en: The text starts spread far apart, blurred and semi-transparent, then, as if pulled in by a magnet, accelerates toward the center, overshoots slightly, and snaps into place; after a pause it spreads apart again. The last two characters use an accent color as the focal point. About 2.8 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: A grid of text expands with a wave
prompt_en: The same character is arranged in an 8×4 grid, expanding in sequence in rings from the center outward, brightening, then shrinking and dimming again, forming a pulsing ripple. About 1.8 seconds per wave, with a rhythmic background feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Thin text gradually grows bolder
prompt_en: The text slowly changes from an extremely thin font weight to the heaviest font weight, pauses, then returns to thin again (a variable-weight font is required). About 3 seconds per cycle, emphasizing the sense of transformation.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: The same character opens out like a fan
prompt_en: The same character is copied 7 times and stacked together, opening out into a fan shape pivoting below the character, pausing, then folding closed again. The center copy is opaque and the rest are semi-transparent. About 3 seconds per cycle, with a Japanese-style entrance feel.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: A small ball bounces, lighting up each character
prompt_en: A small glowing ball jumps to the right above the text, character by character; each time it lands on a character, that character lights up from dim with a glow, like karaoke subtitles. About 0.38 seconds per character; after jumping through the whole line, it starts again.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Swings like a pendulum from a point above
prompt_en: Each character has a small dot at its top, and the character swings left and right like a pendulum from that pivot point by about ±14 degrees, with each character's swinging offset from the others. About 1.7 seconds per swing, lazy and cute.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Turns into blocks, dissolves away, then restores
prompt_en: The text is covered with small squares on top of it; the squares appear randomly, one by one, to hide the text, then disappear one by one to bring the text back, with a few accent-colored squares mixed in, like a pixel dissolve. About 3 seconds per cycle, with a digital feel.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: Switches words inside a ring
prompt_en: The character inside the rounded square at the center switches in sequence (e.g., Spring → Summer → Autumn → Winter), each switch with an up-and-down flipping motion, while a ring of text around it keeps rotating slowly. One switch about every 1.3 seconds.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: Races past trailing afterimages
prompt_en: The text rushes at high speed from outside the left of the screen into the center, leaning in italics, stops briefly, then rushes out to the right, dragging 4 layers of semi-transparent blurred afterimages behind it, while horizontal speed lines flash across the background. About 2.6 seconds per cycle, with a sense of racing speed.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Checkerboard text flips in a wave
prompt_en: The same character is arranged in a 10×4 checkerboard grid, with dark and light blocks alternating, flipping around the Y axis in sequence from top-left to bottom-right, forming a diagonal tile-flipping wave. About 2.6 seconds per cycle, with a patterned background feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Text races along an ∞ track
prompt_en: Each character runs in sequence along a dashed “∞”-shaped track, turning to follow its direction of travel, linked head-to-tail like a little convoy. About 4.5 seconds per lap, with a joyful racing feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Text swaps positions, then lines up neatly
prompt_en: Each character of the text swaps positions randomly with a little bounce and tilt; after shuffling several times in a row, it returns to its place and lines up neatly, pauses, then starts shuffling again. Each swap takes about 0.6 seconds, with a game-puzzle feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Text rotates along a spiral
prompt_en: Text is arranged along a spiral line, gradually growing larger from small characters at the center outward; the whole vortex keeps rotating, and the characters' opacity alternates between bright and dark in turn. About 9 seconds per revolution, with a fantastical drawn-in feel.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: Shakes, then gradually settles
prompt_en: The text first shakes violently left, right, up and down and rotates; the shaking gradually gets smaller until it finally settles and stops, pauses for a while, then starts shaking again. About 2.4 seconds per cycle, with a startled, tense feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Text stretches vertically into a wave
prompt_en: With its base at the bottom, each character stretches vertically in sequence to about 1.7x and then shrinks back, while narrowing horizontally at the same time, forming an elastic wave; the last character uses an accent color. About 1.3 seconds per wave, with a pop-music feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: Ink bleeds into shape
prompt_en: The text is like ink dropped on paper: it starts as a blurred, bleeding blob of ink and gradually converges into a clear, sharp character shape, pauses, then bleeds out and disappears, with each character staggered in sequence. About 3.4 seconds per cycle, with a Japanese-style handwritten feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: Scattered text gathers together
prompt_en: Each character of the text flies in from all over the screen with rotation, blur and enlargement, gathering one by one into its correct position and sharpening into focus, pauses, then scatters apart again. About 3.2 seconds per cycle, with a title-intro feel.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: Different fonts light up in sequence
prompt_en: 8 characters are arranged in a 4×2 grid, each cell using a different font (sans-serif, serif, dot-matrix, rounded, brush, and so on), lighting up inverted and enlarging slightly one cell at a time in sequence, then dimming back down. About 3.2 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: Text crumbles and falls
prompt_en: Each character first tilts slightly, then falls downward in sequence as if crumbling, accelerating under gravity, rotating and fading out, then drops back from above into its original place to reassemble. About 3.4 seconds per cycle, with an ending feel.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: Floats light and airy
prompt_en: Each character floats slowly up, down, left and right at a different speed and rotates slightly, with a soft glow, like a feather drifting lightly. About 3–4.5 seconds per cycle for each character, with a soothing, dreamy feel.
style_en: Letter-by-Letter Motion

desc_en: A word pops out with a thump
prompt_en: The text rapidly pops out from 0, enlarges to 1.25x, then returns to its original size, while a ring of short lines radiates outward from the center, flying apart and disappearing. About 1.8 seconds per cycle, emphasizing the highlight.
style_en: Impact Entrance Canva Style Canva Pop Pop Out

desc_en: Letters slam in one by one
prompt_en: The text slams down into place one character at a time from above at large size, each character squashing slightly and rebounding as it lands, spaced about 0.2 seconds apart in sequence; after all have appeared, they fade out together. About 3 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: Stamped on one by one like a seal
prompt_en: Two stamped texts with thick borders slam down diagonally with a bang from 2.4x size, settling after shrinking back slightly, the stamp faces with a slightly distressed texture, the two stamps coming down in sequence. About 2.8 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Impact Entrance Canva Style Canva Stomp Smash

desc_en: Flies out from deep inside, trailing afterimages behind it
prompt_en: The text rushes forward at high speed from deep in the frame (tiny and blurred), overshooting slightly as it enlarges before rebounding into place, trailing 4 layers of semi-transparent afterimages behind it. About 2.2 seconds per cycle, with a strong opening emphasis.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: Words fly in one by one and stack up
prompt_en: Three lines of words fly in with rotation from the left, right, and below respectively, stacking in sequence into a centered layout, each line at a different font size with the middle line in an accent color; after lingering, they fade out together. About 3.4 seconds per cycle, with an MV lyric feel.
style_en: Impact Entrance

desc_en: Dives into the letters, connects to the next word
prompt_en: A word scales up from small to normal size, then accelerates and enlarges until it fills the frame and fades out, like the camera diving into the letters; the next word then appears from far away to follow. About 1.2 seconds per word.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: Squashes flat like rubber, then swaps the word
prompt_en: The text squashes flat into a line like rubber, then springs up tall and rebounds into place; after pausing, it squashes flat again, swapping to the next word at its flattest point. About 1.5 seconds per cycle, an elastic switch.
style_en: Per-Character Motion

desc_en: Huge text crosses the screen, one fast and one slow
prompt_en: Text at an oversized scale (larger than the frame) continuously drifts slowly from right to left across the frame, while a thin strip at the bottom carries small text sliding faster in the opposite direction. The large text takes about 9 seconds per cycle, giving a distant background feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Vertical text flows in opposite directions
prompt_en: Multiple columns of vertical text, thick and thin columns alternating, adjacent columns flowing in opposite directions — one up, one down — in a serif (Mincho) typeface. The large columns are slow (about 11 seconds), the small columns fast (about 6 seconds), an Eastern sense of stillness and motion.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Diagonal bands, text running in reverse
prompt_en: Two diagonal text bands cross through the frame, distinguished by different background colors, the repeated text on the bands continuously sliding in opposite directions, the bands casting shadows. About 7–9 seconds per cycle, with a playful transition feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Text flows along a wavy line
prompt_en: A wide, semi-transparent wavy ribbon crosses the frame, and text continuously flows forward along the wavy curve. It flows through a segment in about 2.4 seconds, with a decorative, musical rhythm.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Bands with different fonts and speeds layered together
prompt_en: Four horizontal marquee bands layered together, each with a different font, font size, speed, and direction, with thin divider lines between the bands. Speeds vary from 5–11 seconds per cycle, like a street bulletin board.
style_en: Flowing Background
txt_en: Limited Sale New Arrivals Pre-order Last Day

desc_en: Three layers of vertical text flowing together
prompt_en: Three layers of vertical text flowing vertically: the back layer is small, very faint, and fast; the middle layer is semi-transparent at medium speed; the front layer is large, opaque, and slow, creating a parallax depth of field, in a serif (Mincho) typeface. A nighttime Eastern feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Taped text crossed into an X
prompt_en: Two caution tapes with thick borders cross into an X shape, the repeated text on the tapes sliding in opposite directions, with shadows. About 6–8 seconds per cycle, with a warning, cordoned-off feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Pass through the middle of the text
prompt_en: Multiple layered copies of the same word continuously scale up from tiny at the center, growing larger until they rush out of the frame and fade, one layer after another, like passing through a text tunnel, adjacent layers alternating between two color tones. About 3.6 seconds per layer.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: Floor and walls are all text, moving forward all the way
prompt_en: A corridor in 3D perspective, its floor, ceiling, and left and right walls all covered in repeated text, the text continuously flowing toward the viewer, with a dark gradient at the vanishing point in the center. About 6 seconds per cycle, an immersive forward-moving feel.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: Text cylinders rotate in opposite directions
prompt_en: Three 3D cylinders made of text (the same character ringing a full circle), rotating along a horizontal axis, adjacent cylinders in opposite directions, the middle one in an accent color. About 4 seconds per revolution, with a three-dimensional logo feel.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: Rings of text rush toward you
prompt_en: Multiple rings made of text scale up one by one from tiny at the center, rushing toward the viewer and fading out, each ring itself also rotating, adjacent rings in opposite directions. About 4.2 seconds per ring.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: A single word orbits with depth of field
prompt_en: Text circles along an elliptical dashed orbit, growing larger and sharper as it comes to the front and smaller and fainter as it goes to the back, creating depth of field. About 5 seconds per orbit, with a logo title feel.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: A cube with text on four faces flips vertically
prompt_en: A 3D cube with one character written on each of its four faces flips 90 degrees around a horizontal axis each time to switch to the next face, pausing after each flip, at a slightly tilted viewing angle, the cube with thick borders. About 1.5 seconds per face.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: The thickness of 3D letters rotates a full turn
prompt_en: Thick 3D extruded text, its front brighter and its sides built from multiple layers of shading from dark to light to form the thickness; the whole set of letters slowly rotates a full turn around a vertical axis, letting the side thickness be seen. About 5 seconds per revolution.
style_en: 3D Spatial Rotation

desc_en: Flips into place like a station timetable
prompt_en: Each character sits in a split-flap cell (with a divider line in the middle) and, like a station timetable, rapidly flips through many random characters, stopping in sequence from left to right on the correct character; after lingering, it flips again. The flipping is fast, with everything settled in about 1.5 seconds.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: Cards flip over one by one to change the text
prompt_en: Each character is a card that flips in sequence around the Y axis, front and back in contrasting color schemes; after flipping into another set of text it lingers, then flips back. About 3.4 seconds per cycle, with an announcement-switching feel.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: Typed out character by character, then replaced
prompt_en: Text appears over two lines character by character like a typewriter, with a blinking cursor behind it; after finishing and lingering, it is quickly deleted character by character and the next sentence is typed. Serif (Mincho) typeface, the second line fainter, typing at about 0.14 seconds per character.
style_en: Text Switching Canva Style Canva Typewriter Typewriter

desc_en: Reels spin and come to a stop
prompt_en: Each character sits in a slot-machine reel window (the windows have inner shadows at the top and bottom); the reels rapidly scroll upward through many random characters, then slow down and stop in sequence from left to right on the result characters (with a slight rebound); after lingering, they spin again. About 4 seconds per cycle.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: Numbers scroll upward and increase
prompt_en: For numbers such as 'Cumulative total: 12,480 people', each digit sits in a small cell, the numbers scrolling upward and incrementing like an odometer, with a slight rebound. It increases about once every 1 second.
style_en: Text Switching

desc_en: News headlines swap one for another
prompt_en: A 'Breaking News' label stays fixed on the left, while news headlines in the frame on the right slide in from below as the old headline slides out upward, one replacing another. A new headline about every 1.6 seconds.
style_en: Text Switching
txt_en: Fully Free Live Tonight 3 Days Only

desc_en: Electronic text made of dots
prompt_en: Text made of a dot matrix like an electronic billboard, continuously scrolling from right to left, with clear contrast between lit and unlit dots. Medium scrolling speed, with a retro tech feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Hollow text fills up line by line
prompt_en: The frame is covered with multiple lines of repeated outlined hollow text, each line slowly shifting horizontally in a different direction, and filling with color line by line from top to bottom before returning to hollow. About 3.2 seconds per cycle, with a textured MV feel.
style_en: Flowing Background

desc_en: Large text is cut into several offset slices
prompt_en: The large text is normally still, but occasionally it suddenly cuts into 6 horizontal slices, each slice offset randomly left or right with chromatic aberration (RGB split), flashing once before recovering, at an irregular frequency. The glitch flickers about every 0.1 seconds, with an impactful MV feel.
style_en: Dissipating Exit

desc_en: Text becomes a window, stripes flow through inside
prompt_en: The text is like a window, filled inside with diagonal stripes alternating in two colors, the stripes continuously flowing sideways. Bold typeface, flowing through one stripe cycle in about 1 second, with a playful festival feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: A long, long shadow turns a full circle
prompt_en: A very long flat shadow trails behind the text, the shadow's direction continuously rotating a full circle around the text. About 7 seconds per revolution, in a flat design style.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: Hollow text is slowly filled with liquid
prompt_en: At first there is only outlined hollow text; liquid slowly fills the letters from bottom to top; after filling and lingering, it empties and starts over. About 3.4 seconds per cycle, with a fresh MV feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: A highlighter sweeps across behind the text
prompt_en: For text on a card, a highlighter line sweeps from left to right behind the lower half of the letters, lingers, then fades out. The sweep takes about 1 second, the whole cycle about 3 seconds, with an emphasis-and-commentary feel.
style_en: Textured Fill

desc_en: A diagonal line sweeps across and the two areas swap
prompt_en: The frame is divided into two areas by a diagonal line, the two areas' background and text colors in contrast with each other; the diagonal line sweeps across the frame from left to right, swapping the text's two color schemes. One sweep about every 3.4 seconds, with a title-switching feel.
style_en: Text Switching Canva Style Canva Block Block

desc_en: Each character slides up from below a mask
prompt_en: The text is split into individual characters, each placed inside a clipping mask, sliding up in sequence from below the mask (about 0.06 seconds between characters, with strong deceleration); after lingering, they slide out upward. (GSAP: SplitText with type chars + mask, from yPercent: 110, ease power4.out, stagger)
style_en: Canva Style Canva Ascend Rise Rise

desc_en: Scrambled characters gradually resolve into the correct text
prompt_en: The text starts as a string of constantly jittering scrambled characters (katakana, symbols, numbers) and gradually resolves into the correct text from left to right, the scrambled characters and the resolved ones distinguished by different colors; after lingering, it scrambles again. Dot-matrix typeface. (GSAP: ScrambleTextPlugin, revealDelay, speed, newClass)

desc_en: Type, delete, swap to the next sentence
prompt_en: Like a typewriter, type out a sentence character by character, the cursor blinking behind it; after lingering for about 1 second, delete it character by character from the end, then type the next sentence, cycling through three sentences. (GSAP: TextPlugin typing + a timeline chaining the deletions)
style_en: Canva Style Canva Typewriter Typewriter

desc_en: Letters fall from the sky and wobble elastically
prompt_en: Each character drops from above the frame in random order, with random rotation, wobbling elastically like jelly as it lands before settling into place; after lingering, they all drop down and fade out together. (GSAP: SplitText chars, ease elastic.out(1,0.35), stagger from random)
style_en: Canva Style Canva Bounce Bounce

desc_en: Each character enters flipping around the X axis
prompt_en: Each character enters with a 3D flip around the X axis (flipping from the back to the front, with a slight rebound), spaced 0.07 seconds apart in sequence; after lingering, it flips forward and disappears. (GSAP: SplitText chars, rotationX, transformOrigin with Z depth, ease back.out)

desc_en: Letters fly in from everywhere, then scatter apart
prompt_en: Each character flies in from random positions all over the frame, with random rotation and size, decelerating strongly to assemble into the text; after lingering, it bursts apart to random positions. (GSAP: SplitText chars, "random(-400,400)" function-based values, ease expo, stagger from random)

desc_en: Cells scale in waves outward from the center
prompt_en: The same character is arranged in a 10×5 grid, shrinking, rotating, and fading in waves outward from the center, then enlarging and rotating back inward from the edges, forming a ripple. (GSAP: stagger { grid: [5,10], from: "center" / "edges", amount: 1 })

desc_en: A fixed prefix, with the word after it rotating through replacements
prompt_en: A fixed prefix "We make", with the word after it rotating inside a mask: each new word slides up letter by letter from below, stays for a while, then slides up and out, followed by the next word; the rotating words use the accent color. (GSAP: SplitText chars + mask, a timeline chains each word in sequence)

desc_en: Numbers count up in a rolling fashion while a progress bar fills in sync
prompt_en: The large number below the label quickly counts up from 0 to 128,450, slowing down as it gets closer to the end, while the progress bar below fills in sync; after a pause it fades out and starts over, with the number in tabular figures. (GSAP: tween an object's value + onUpdate writes it with toLocaleString, ease power3.out)

desc_en: Letters are pushed away as the cursor approaches
prompt_en: When the cursor comes near the text, nearby letters are pushed outward and switch to the accent color — the closer the cursor, the farther they are pushed — and when the cursor leaves, they smoothly return to their original positions. (GSAP: SplitText chars, each letter's x/y controlled with gsap.quickTo, with the push force calculated from the cursor distance)

desc_en: Lines flip up one by one from beneath a mask
prompt_en: Multiple lines of text flip up one by one from beneath their own masks, with a slight rotation, the last line in the accent color; a thin line below is drawn from left to right, and after a pause the whole block sweeps upward and away. (GSAP: each line wrapped in overflow hidden, from yPercent:115, stagger 0.14)

desc_en: Squashes flat on landing, stretches on rebound
prompt_en: The text drops from above, squashing flat like rubber when it lands and stretching out as it rebounds, bouncing a few times before coming to rest, while the ground shadow scales with its height. (GSAP: CustomBounce.create generates two eases, bounce and squash, applied to y and to scaleX/scaleY respectively)

desc_en: A hand-drawn circle and underline are drawn in
prompt_en: A hand-drawn-style line draws a circle around the key text, then draws an underline beneath it; after a pause, the lines retract in the direction of their starting point, with round line caps. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin, drawSVG "0%"→"100%", then to "100% 100%")

desc_en: Circle, star, heart and cloud morph into each other
prompt_en: A block of color smoothly morphs between a circle, a star, a heart and a cloud, changing to a different color with each morph, while the whole thing rotates slowly. (GSAP: MorphSVGPlugin, morphSVG switches the paths, ease expo.inOut)

desc_en: A paper plane flies along a curve, turning as it goes
prompt_en: A paper plane flies across the screen along a dashed curve with a loop, its nose turning to follow the path's direction, and starts over after it flies off-screen. (GSAP: MotionPathPlugin, path/align specify the SVG path, autoRotate:true)

desc_en: Smoothly rearranges between a grid and a single row
prompt_en: 8 blocks switch between two layouts — a "4×2 grid" and "a single row" — while their order is randomly shuffled at the same time; each block smoothly slides to its new position and new size. (GSAP: Flip.getState to record → change the class and DOM order → Flip.from to tween)

desc_en: Fades in when scrolled to, with the progress bar in sync
prompt_en: In a scrollable region, the progress bar at the top fills in proportion to scrolling; each paragraph of text fades in from the left when it is scrolled to 85% of the viewport, and fades out again when scrolling back up. (GSAP: ScrollTrigger toggleActions "play none none reverse", the progress bar uses scrub:true)

desc_en: Scroll down, and the content slides left
prompt_en: When scrolling down, a whole row of work cards instead slides horizontally to the left, so that scrolling to the very bottom lands exactly on the last card, like a horizontal portfolio showcase. (GSAP: ScrollTrigger pin (or sticky) + scrub, the x travel distance = track width − viewport width)

desc_en: Far, middle and near layers move at different speeds
prompt_en: When scrolling, large background text in the far layer, dots in the middle layer and the title in the near layer move up and down at different speeds — the near layer fastest, the far layer slowest — creating depth-of-field parallax. (GSAP: one timeline bound to a ScrollTrigger with scrub, the three layers each set to a different yPercent range)

desc_en: The button is pulled toward the cursor and springs back
prompt_en: When the cursor approaches the button, the button is pulled toward the cursor's direction, while the text inside the button moves less, creating a layered effect, and it switches to the accent color at the same time; when the cursor leaves, it returns to its original position with elasticity. (GSAP: gsap.quickTo controls x/y, ease elastic.out(1,0.4))

desc_en: Trailing dots and an inverted-color circle
prompt_en: Behind the cursor follows a string of trailing dots, from fast to slow, plus a larger circle laid over the text in an inverted-color blend mode, so the text turns inverted in color as it passes over. (GSAP: multiple gsap.quickTo with different durations, the large circle uses mix-blend-mode:difference)

desc_en: Cards can be dragged and tossed with inertia
prompt_en: Several cards can be dragged with the mouse or a finger; on release they glide with inertia according to the toss velocity, decelerating and bouncing back at the boundaries, and the card being dragged floats to the top layer. (GSAP: Draggable.create { bounds, inertia:true, edgeResistance }, requires InertiaPlugin)

desc_en: Cards are dealt from the bottom and unfold into a fan
prompt_en: 5 cards are dealt in sequence from the bottom of the screen, unfolding into an angled fan with a slight rebound, and after a pause they are gathered back to the bottom, starting from the last card. (GSAP: timeline + stagger, xPercent / rotation use function values (i)=>(i-2)*115)

desc_en: A burst of confetti affected by gravity
prompt_en: As the text elastically scales up, a large handful of paper pieces bursts out from below; the pieces fall in gravity-driven parabolas, rotating and fading out toward the end, once every 2 seconds. (GSAP: Physics2DPlugin velocity / angle / gravity, randomized with random)

desc_en: The wheel or dragging speeds up the marquee and tilts it
prompt_en: Two lines of infinite marquee (one solid, one hollow outline, running in opposite directions); when the user scrolls the wheel or drags, they speed up and tilt according to the direction, and after stopping they slowly return to their original speed. (GSAP: Observer obtains velocityY, adjusting tween.timeScale and skewX)

desc_en: Side navigation dots light up with scrolling; click one to jump to that section
prompt_en: Scroll navigation / side navigation dots (Scroll Spy / Dot Navigation, also called anchor navigation or page progress navigation): a row of small dots is fixed on the right side of the page, each dot corresponding to one section; whichever section is scrolled to, its corresponding dot enlarges and fills with the accent color, with a pill label showing that section's name floating out beside it; between the dots there is a thin track, and the progress bar inside the track grows downward in proportion to the whole page's scrolling; clicking any dot smoothly scrolls to that section, and hovering the mouse over a dot also shows its name. The sections alternate between light and dark background shades. (GSAP: one ScrollTrigger per section, start "top center", end "bottom center", onToggle toggles active; the progress bar uses scaleY with scrub:true; clicking uses gsap.to(scroller,{scrollTop}) or ScrollToPlugin)
style_en: Scroll Navigation Side Navigation Dots Anchor Navigation Page Progress Navigation Scroll Spy Navigation Dot Navigation

desc_en: On hover the letters roll up one by one, the button inverts, and the arrow turns
prompt_en: A pill-shaped button, with text on the left and a circular arrow on the right. When the mouse moves over it, each letter of the button text rolls upward in sequence (each letter delayed by about 0.035 seconds), with an identical copy of the text filling in from below; at the same time, the button's background and text colors swap to the accent scheme, the circle on the right also inverts its colors, and the arrow rotates to point up-right at 45 degrees; when the mouse leaves, everything rolls back in reverse. The whole thing takes about 0.55 seconds, with ease-in-out (cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1)). (CSS: each letter wrapped in a span, ::after{content:attr(data-t);top:100%} creates the second copy of the text, the outer layer has overflow:hidden, on :hover translateY(-100%), and transition-delay uses calc(var(--i)*.035s) to stagger the letters)
style_en: Button hover Hover Rolling Text Roll Text Button Hover Stagger CTA

desc_en: Spreads to fill from the point where the mouse entered, and retracts toward the exit point on leave
prompt_en: An outlined pill button. When the mouse moves in, an accent-colored circle enlarges starting from "the exact point where the cursor entered the button", spreading until it fills the whole button, while the text color switches at the same time to a color that contrasts with the fill; when the mouse moves out, the circle shrinks away centered on "the point where the cursor left", so the color retracts toward whichever side it exits from. About 0.55 seconds, ease-in-out. (How it works: the button has overflow:hidden; on pointerenter / pointerleave, getBoundingClientRect is used to calculate the cursor's coordinates inside the button and write them into the CSS variables --x and --y, the circle's diameter is taken as "distance to the farthest corner × 2" to ensure full coverage; the circle uses transform:scale(0→1) as a transition)
style_en: Button hover Direction-aware Spread Fill Ripple From Mouse Position Direction Aware Hover Fill Ripple Button CTA

desc_en: A group of cards floats up in sequence from top-left to bottom-right, going from blurry to clear
prompt_en: Work cards in 3 columns × 2 rows (a thumbnail on top, a title and two lines of text below); on entrance, each card floats up from a state 30px below, at 95% size, blurred and transparent, becoming clear, in a sequence staggered diagonally from top-left to bottom-right (about 0.6 seconds in total); the thumbnail, title and text lines inside each card then catch up one by one with a slight extra delay; after a pause, they fade out upward in reverse, starting from the last card. Ease-out (power3.out). (GSAP: stagger { grid:[2,3], from:"start", amount:0.6 }, fromTo y / opacity / scale / filter:blur; on a real site, pair this with ScrollTrigger so it plays when scrolled into view, or use ScrollTrigger.batch to bring lists in in batches)
style_en: Card Group List Entrance In Sequence Staggered Emerge Fade In Stagger Fade Up Grid Reveal List Entrance
txt_en: Brand Website App Poster Packaging Illustration

desc_en: On hover the image tilts in 3D following the cursor, with layered parallax scenery, a glare, and a caption sliding out
prompt_en: An image card: when the mouse moves over the image, the whole image tilts in 3D in the direction of the cursor position (up to about ±10 degrees) and scales up slightly; the far, middle and near scenery inside the image shift in the opposite direction at different rates, forming parallax depth; a soft glare follows the cursor; at the same time, the caption text at the bottom (a small label + a title) slides up from below. When the mouse leaves, everything smoothly returns upright and the caption retracts. (GSAP: gsap.quickTo controls rotationX / rotationY / scale, the parent layer has perspective set; each layer is displaced with quickTo at a different coefficient; the glare uses a radial-gradient positioned with the CSS variables --gx and --gy; the caption uses a transform transition)
style_en: Image Photo hover Hover 3D Tilt Parallax Glare Tilt Parallax Glare Image Hover Card

desc_en: Several blurred glows drift and blend slowly, flowing like an aurora
prompt_en: In a Hero section background, place 3–4 large circular glows that overlap and blend into each other after heavy blurring, each slowly drifting, scaling up and down and swaying back and forth at a different speed (about 9–16 seconds), forming a gradient that keeps flowing like an aurora; the foreground title stays clear and readable. (CSS: each glow is a large circle + filter:blur + mix-blend-mode:screen, each set to a different animation-duration and a negative animation-delay, with animation-direction:alternate)
style_en: Background Aurora Gradient Glow Aurora Mesh Gradient Blob Glow Hero Background

desc_en: A fine grid-line background, with the grid lines near the cursor lit up with a soft glow
prompt_en: The background of the whole section is a faint fine grid; the ring of grid lines around the cursor's position lights up in the accent color, with a soft glow, the lit area following the cursor and fading out naturally at the edges; when the cursor leaves, the lit area disappears. (How it works: two identical grid-line background layers, the upper layer in the accent color, then mask:radial-gradient(circle at var(--mx) var(--my)) reveals only the area near the cursor; --mx and --my are updated on mousemove)
style_en: Background Grid Grid Lines Spotlight Cursor Glow Spotlight Grid Pattern Cursor Glow SaaS

desc_en: Floating particles automatically connect when close; the cursor attracts nearby particles
prompt_en: Dozens of small particles in the background drift slowly and randomly, bouncing off the boundaries; when two particles are close enough they automatically connect with a line — the closer they are, the clearer the line, the farther, the fainter; when the cursor moves in, nearby particles are gently drawn toward it and connect to it, forming an effect like a constellation network. The foreground title stays clear. (Canvas 2D: requestAnimationFrame updates the positions every frame, lines are drawn by computing pairwise distances with opacity adjusted by distance; note the canvas size should be set according to devicePixelRatio)
style_en: Background Particles Connecting Lines Network Constellation Particles Network Constellation particles.js Canvas

desc_en: A diagonal sheen sweeps across the button on a timer; on hover it speeds up and the button lifts
prompt_en: On a solid button there is a diagonal translucent highlight that quickly sweeps from left to right about every 2.4 seconds, like a reflection on metal or glass; when the mouse moves over it, the sheen sweeps faster, and the button lifts slightly while its shadow deepens at the same time. (CSS: the button has overflow:hidden, ::after creates a gradient highlight band with skewX(-20deg), and keyframes change its left position; :hover shortens the animation-duration and adds translateY)
style_en: Button Sheen Reflection Light Sweep Flash Shine Sweep Glint Shimmer Button CTA

desc_en: The gradient light on the button's border keeps rotating around it, with a soft outer glow
prompt_en: The border of a pill button is a ring of multicolored gradient light, and the gradient keeps rotating around the border (about 3 seconds per revolution), with a layer of blurred soft glow behind the border; inside the button are a solid background and text; when the mouse moves over it, the rotation speeds up. (CSS: @property registers the angle variable --ang, the background uses conic-gradient(from var(--ang)), and keyframes rotate --ang to 360deg; an inner span covers the middle so only the border shows; ::before duplicates the background and blurs it for the outer glow)
style_en: Button Border Gradient Rotation Glow Glow Border Conic Gradient Animated Border Button

desc_en: Clicking the heart makes it bounce and scale up, spraying small dots and a ring of light around it
prompt_en: When the "Like" button is clicked, the hollow heart instantly fills and bounces up from small to large, while 8 small dots spray outward from around the heart and a ring of light expands and disappears, and the number beside it goes +1; clicking again cancels it, the heart returns to hollow and the number goes −1. The whole thing takes about 0.5 seconds, with an elastic feedback feel. (CSS: toggling the .on class; the heart uses a scale bounce keyframes, the small dots use rotate(var(--r)) translateY to fly outward while shrinking and fading, the ring uses scale + opacity; before replaying, remove the class first and trigger a reflow)
style_en: Button Like Favorite Heart Click Feedback Micro-interaction Like Heart Burst Micro-interaction Twitter

desc_en: On hover the card lifts and its shadow deepens, and the thumbnail zooms inside its frame
prompt_en: A row of work cards (a thumbnail on top, a title and a line of text below). When the mouse moves over a card, the card lifts up a little and a deeper, larger shadow appears, and the thumbnail slowly zooms to about 1.15× inside its original frame (the frame stays the same, the image is cropped); when the mouse leaves, it smoothly returns to its original position. About 0.45–0.6 seconds, ease-out. (CSS: the card transitions transform and box-shadow, on :hover translateY(-8px); the thumbnail's frame has overflow:hidden, and the inner image uses transform:scale(1.14))
style_en: Card hover Lift Shadow Thumbnail Zoom Hover Lift Card Shadow Zoom Portfolio Product

desc_en: As the cursor passes, the card's border and interior are lit by a pool of light
prompt_en: A row of understated cards: when the cursor moves near a card, the stretch of the card's border closest to the cursor is lit by a pool of light (in the accent color), and inside the card there is also a very faint glow following the cursor; the light only illuminates the area near the cursor and gets darker the farther away it is, so the edges of neighboring cards can also be seen faintly lit at the same time. (How it works: on mousemove, calculate the cursor's coordinates relative to each card and write them into --x and --y; ::before uses radial-gradient(circle at var(--x) var(--y)) with mask-composite to show only the border ring, and ::after creates the soft interior glow)
style_en: Card Glow Border Spotlight Cursor Glow Spotlight Card Glow Border Linear Vercel

desc_en: A skeleton is shown before the content loads; after a sheen sweeps across, the real content fades in
prompt_en: While the data is loading, the card first shows a low-contrast skeleton: a circular avatar, two text bars of different lengths, and a large image area, with a soft highlight continuously sweeping across the skeleton from left to right; when loading completes, the skeleton fades out, and the real avatar, title, time and image fade in while sliding slightly upward into place. (CSS: the skeleton elements use a linear-gradient highlight band + background-size:300%, with keyframes moving the background-position; when loading completes, a class is switched so the skeleton goes to opacity 0 and the content to opacity 1 + a translateY transition)
style_en: Skeleton Loading Reading Placeholder Skeleton Loading Shimmer Placeholder Loader

desc_en: The image is uncovered from bottom to top, while scaling down from enlarged to its original size
prompt_en: When the image enters, its frame is uncovered from bottom to top like a curtain, while the picture inside the frame slowly scales down from about 1.35× to its original size, creating the layers of "uncovering + camera pulling back"; after a pause, it is then gathered up and disappears from bottom to top. The uncovering takes about 1.2 seconds, ease-in-out (cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1)). (CSS: the frame uses clip-path:inset() keyframes from inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0); the inner image uses transform:scale 1.35→1; on a real site, this can be played only when scrolled into view)
style_en: Image Photo Mask Reveal Entrance clip-path Image Reveal Mask Wipe Zoom

desc_en: Drag the handle in the middle to compare the difference between two images, left and right
prompt_en: Two images of the same size overlap, with a straight line and a circular handle (with left and right arrows) in the middle, BEFORE marked in the top-left corner and AFTER in the top-right; when the handle is dragged, the dividing line moves left and right with it, the left side showing the original image and the right side the edited image, making the differences easy to compare; when not operated, it can sway slowly left and right to hint that it is draggable. (How it works: the upper image uses clip-path:inset(0 0 0 var(--p)), on pointerdown/pointermove the cursor's proportion inside the frame is calculated and written into --p; the handle uses setPointerCapture to ensure dragging continues even when dragged outside the frame; on mobile, set touch-action:pan-y)
style_en: Image Comparison Contrast Before and After Slider Drag Before After Compare Slider Image Comparison

desc_en: When scrolling down, the navigation bar gets shorter, the Logo shrinks, and a frosted-glass background is added
prompt_en: The header navigation bar is fixed at the very top (sticky). At the top of the page the navigation bar is taller, the Logo is larger and the background is transparent; as soon as you scroll down past a certain distance, the navigation bar smoothly becomes shorter, the Logo shrinks, and a translucent frosted-glass background and a faint shadow appear; scrolling back to the top restores the original state. About a 0.35-second transition. (How it works: listen to scroll, and add a .shrink class when scrollY exceeds a certain value; CSS transitions padding, font-size, background and box-shadow, with the background using backdrop-filter:blur)
style_en: Navigation Bar Header Menu header navbar Scroll Shrink Sticky Frosted Glass Sticky Shrink Header On Scroll

desc_en: Notifications pop in and stack from the bottom-right corner in sequence, then slide out and disappear after a few seconds
prompt_en: When an operation completes, a notification pops up in the bottom-right corner of the screen (a checkmark in a circle icon on the left, a message in the middle, a "just now" time on the right), entering from below with a slight scale and elastic feel; a new notification stacks below, pushing the old ones up; at most 3 are shown at the same time, and each one slides out to the right and fades away after about 3.4 seconds, with the remaining notifications smoothly moving up to fill the gap. (CSS + JS: the notification wrapper uses display:grid + grid-template-rows 1fr→0fr to collapse the height so filling the gap is smooth; entrance uses keyframes translateY + scale; for exit, add an .out class and then remove the element)
style_en: Notification Prompt Message Toast Pop-up Toast Notification Snackbar Alert Stack

desc_en: A small dot cursor expands into a circle with text in it when moved over a work
prompt_en: Hide the system cursor and use a small dot that follows the mouse instead (with a slight lag); when the cursor moves over a work thumbnail, the small dot smoothly expands into a circle about 3× larger, with prompt text such as "VIEW" appearing in the center of the circle, and the work itself shrinks slightly in response; when leaving the work, it shrinks back to a small dot and the text fades out. The expansion takes about 0.35 seconds, ease-out. (How it works: the container is set to cursor:none; the custom cursor uses position:fixed + transform to follow mousemove; when hovering a target, add a class so the inner circle goes scale(0.16→1) and the text opacity 0→1; this effect should be disabled on touch devices)
style_en: Cursor Custom Cursor Enlarge Hover VIEW View Custom Cursor Hover Expand Portfolio

desc_en: When skimming a work list, a preview image floats out following the cursor and tilts as it moves
prompt_en: A large-text work list (each row has the work's name on the left and its number on the right, with thin divider lines between rows), with unselected rows in fainter text; when the cursor slides onto a row, that row's text becomes clear and pushes slightly to the right, while a preview image of that work scales up from small and floats beside the cursor, following its movement — the faster it moves left or right, the more the image tilts in the direction of movement; when moving to another row, the preview image changes to another one, and when leaving the list, the image shrinks and fades out. (How it works: the preview image uses position:absolute + pointer-events:none, on mousemove it is translated to the cursor position, its rotate is calculated from the horizontal velocity with an upper limit; image switching uses opacity / scale transitions)
style_en: Cursor List List Preview Image Emerge Follow Hover Image Reveal List Preview Follow Cursor Portfolio
txt_en: Brand Identity Website Design Packaging Illustration

desc_en: A line trails behind the cursor, growing thinner and fainter
prompt_en: When the cursor moves, a smooth line trails behind it — thicker and clearer the closer it is to the cursor, thinner and more transparent toward the tail, like a comet's tail; when the cursor stops, the tail gradually retracts to the cursor's position; the cursor itself is a small dot. (Canvas 2D: each frame, push the cursor coordinates into an array and keep only the most recent ~28 points, draw line segments in sequence, with line width and opacity increasing with the index; set the canvas size according to devicePixelRatio; the container uses cursor:none)
style_en: Cursor Trail Trajectory Line Afterimage Cursor Trail Line Comet Canvas

desc_en: Clicking anywhere on screen spreads a ripple from the click point
prompt_en: When clicking anywhere inside the section, a translucent solid circle and an outline ring spread out from the click point at the same time (the outline ring slightly later, by 0.12 seconds), both scaling from 0 up to several times the size of a thumb and fading out, in about 0.85 seconds with strong deceleration, giving the user clear click feedback; rapid repeated clicks are possible, and the ripples overlap. (How it works: on pointerdown, create circular elements at the click coordinates, CSS keyframes do scale(0→1) + opacity(1→0), and the elements are removed when the animation ends)
style_en: Cursor Click Ripple Wave Feedback Click Ripple Wave Feedback Material

desc_en: A ring of text keeps rotating around the cursor
prompt_en: Hide the system cursor and replace it with a small dot, surrounded by a ring of text arranged along a circle (for example "SCROLL · EXPLORE ·" repeated); the text ring keeps rotating slowly (about 8 seconds per revolution), and the whole assembly follows the cursor with a slight lag; the large background heading stays very faint, making the cursor the focus. (How it works: an SVG circular path + textPath, using textLength so the text exactly fills one revolution; the outer layer's transform follows the cursor, and the inner svg uses a CSS rotation animation)
style_en: Cursor Text Ring Circular Text Rotation Circular Text Rotating Text Ring Circular Text Cursor Badge SCROLL

desc_en: The screen is dark, with hidden content lit up only near the cursor, like a flashlight
prompt_en: The whole section is almost dark, with the big headline only faintly visible; wherever the cursor is, it lights up a soft-edged circular area like a flashlight, and inside that area a brighter version hidden underneath is revealed (a clear headline and gradient background). The flashlight follows the cursor, revealing wherever it shines. (How to: two stacked layers with the same layout; the top layer is the vivid version, using mask: radial-gradient(circle at var(--mx) var(--my), #000 55%, transparent) to show only the area near the cursor; update --mx and --my on mousemove)
style_en: Cursor Flashlight Searchlight Spotlight Reveal Mask Flashlight Spotlight Reveal Mask Cursor Hidden

desc_en: Elements in a section gently appear from top to bottom in reading order
prompt_en: When a content section (kicker, main heading, two lines of body copy, and a button) enters, each element gently rises from about 18px below and fully transparent and fades in, following top-to-bottom reading order, with about 0.14 seconds between elements, about 0.9 seconds each, easing out smoothly (power2.out), with no bounce and no scaling, so the eye is naturally led from the heading to the button. (GSAP: fromTo y:18 / opacity:0 → y:0 / opacity:1, stagger 0.14; on a real site, pair it with ScrollTrigger to play once when the section enters the viewport)
style_en: Section Paragraph Heading Rise Fade In Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy Canva Style Canva Rise Rise

desc_en: A paragraph becomes clear line by line from a slight blur, setting a reading rhythm
prompt_en: When a multi-line passage enters, each line in turn slowly becomes clear and fades in from about 10px below, slightly blurred and transparent, with about 0.28 seconds between lines (slower than a typical stagger, close to reading speed), about 1.1 seconds per line, easing out smoothly. The overall feel is quiet and breathable, suited to a brand philosophy or quote section. (GSAP: one element per line or SplitText with type lines, fromTo y:10 / opacity:0 / filter:blur(4px) → clear, stagger 0.28, ease power2.out)
style_en: Paragraph Body Line-by-Line Blur Copy Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy Canva Style Canva Fade Clarify Fade In Clear
txt_en: Good motion doesn't grab attention it gently guides your gaze to the next step

desc_en: A line extends downward, and each step appears as the line reaches it
prompt_en: A vertical timeline: a thin line on the left slowly extends downward from the top (about 2.4 seconds, ease-in-out); whenever the line extends to a node, that node's dot, heading, and description row gently slide in and fade in from about 10px to the left, letting the eye follow the line all the way down through the process. (GSAP: the line scaleY 0→1, with transform-origin at the top; each node does fromTo x:-10 / opacity:0 at its corresponding time point; on a real site, ScrollTrigger scrub can be used so the line's length follows scroll progress)
style_en: Timeline Process Steps Journey Line Extend Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy

desc_en: A homepage layout appears in sequence following a Z-pattern reading order
prompt_en: When a homepage hero enters, the elements fade in and rise in sequence following a Z-pattern reading path: logo at top left → navigation menu at top right → main heading and body copy on the left → hero image on the right → call-to-action button at bottom left → secondary link at bottom right. Each element is spaced about 0.4 seconds apart, rising gently from about 12px below, with an even rhythm and no exaggerated displacement, so the user's gaze moves in the designed order. (The thin lines in the preview only illustrate the Z path and are not needed on a real site. GSAP: arrange the elements in an array in reading order, fromTo y:12 / opacity:0, stagger 0.42, ease power2.out)
style_en: Homepage Hero Layout Z Shape F Shape Reading Pattern Logo Navigation Image Action Button Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy

desc_en: After the connector line between step cards draws across, the next step appears
prompt_en: Three step cards arranged horizontally (numbers 01, 02, 03 + a heading + one line of description). On entry, the first card fades in from about 14px below, then a thin connector line draws from left to right to the second card, which only then fades in, then the line draws to the third card, which fades in; the rhythm is steady, so users clearly understand 'what to do first, then what.' (GSAP: a timeline chained in sequence; cards fromTo y:14 / opacity:0, connector lines scaleX 0→1 with transform-origin on the left, ease power1.inOut / power2.out)
style_en: Steps Process 1 2 3 Connector Line Tutorial Checkout Onboarding Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy
txt_en: Choose a Plan Enter Details Complete Payment

desc_en: After the content appears, a halo gently spreads around the button, drawing the eye to it
prompt_en: A content section (heading, two lines of body copy, and a button) first fades in and rises gently in sequence; about 0.3 seconds after everything has appeared, a translucent halo softly spreads out from around the call-to-action button and fades away, twice in a row, while the button lifts slightly by 3px and returns to place, as if gently reminding 'the next step is here,' then stays still without flashing continuously. (GSAP: first a staggered fade-in, then tween the CSS variable --ring 0→1 to control the spread and opacity of the ::after box-shadow, repeat:1; the whole sequence plays only once)
style_en: CTA Call to Action Button Cue Halo Diffusion Attention Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy

desc_en: An image is revealed from left to right by a soft gradient edge
prompt_en: When an image enters, a gradient mask with a feathered edge slowly sweeps from left to right, softly revealing the image (not a hard straight cut), while the image slowly settles back to its original size and position from 1.08x, slightly left of place, over about 1.9–2.3 seconds, easing out smoothly — quieter and more refined than a hard-edged mask. (CSS + GSAP: the outer frame uses mask:linear-gradient(90deg, #000 var(--p), transparent calc(var(--p) + 25%)); use GSAP to tween --p from -25 to 100; the inner image scale 1.08→1, x -8→0)
style_en: Image Photo Mask Soft Edge Gradient Reveal Feather Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy

desc_en: Figure-and-text rows appear alternating left and right, the gaze moving down in a Z pattern
prompt_en: Figure-and-text rows stacked vertically, alternating left and right (first row image left / text right, second row image right / text left, and so on). On entry they appear top to bottom in sequence, each row gently sliding in about 20px inward from its own side and fading in, spaced about 0.35 seconds apart, about 0.9 seconds per row, easing out smoothly, so the gaze reads downward in a Z pattern. (GSAP: fromTo x alternating ±20 by index / opacity:0, stagger 0.35, ease power2.out; on a real site, ScrollTrigger.batch can be used so each row appears only when scrolled to)
style_en: Image and Text List Left and Right Alternating Z Shape Downward Intro Features Gentle Soft Light Guidance Flow Gaze Reading Order Low-key Subtle Gentle Soft Entrance Visual Flow Hierarchy

desc_en: Upload your own line SVG and watch it drawn stroke by stroke, as if by a pen
prompt_en: Turn the line SVG I provide (pasted after these instructions) into a 'drawn with a pen' entrance: each path is traced one after another in its original drawing order, with each stroke's drawing time allocated by length (longer lines draw longer, shorter ones quicker), the strokes slightly overlapping as they connect, about 3 seconds overall, ease-in-out; after finishing, it can hold then fade out and replay, or play only once. All shapes are changed to stroke only, no fill, with round line caps and joins. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin; for each path / line / polyline / circle, fromTo drawSVG "0%"→"100%" in sequence, with duration calculated in proportion to getTotalLength(); pure CSS can also do this with stroke-dasharray + stroke-dashoffset)
style_en: SVG Upload Custom Line Stroke Hand-drawn Stroke Logo Illustration Line Drawing Stroke Draw Upload Custom

desc_en: A pen tip writes along a signature path, finishing with an underline
prompt_en: A cursive signature line path is slowly written out starting from where the pen first touches, with a small round pen tip following at the very front of the path, as if someone is really writing (about 2.6 seconds, ease-in-out); once the signature is finished, the pen tip disappears and a slightly curved underline is quickly drawn underneath to finish. Suited to a portfolio hero or brand signature. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin draws the signature path while MotionPathPlugin moves the pen-tip dot along the same path, with identical timing and ease for both; the signature must be a single-stroke outline path, not outlined letterforms)
style_en: Signature Handwriting Cursive Writing Pen Tip Signature Handwriting Cursive Pen Write On

desc_en: A line illustration is drawn stroke by stroke, then the main subject softly appears
prompt_en: A line illustration made of multiple lines (for example, a cup of coffee giving off steam: the saucer, cup body, handle, and three wisps of steam) is traced one stroke at a time in order from bottom to top, from the main subject to the details, about 0.9 seconds per stroke with about 0.32 seconds between strokes; once all are drawn, the main subject is softly given a layer of translucent fill, and the steam lines drift gently up and down once. Quiet overall, with a handmade feel. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin staggers the drawing across the paths; the fill uses another path of the same shape fading in from opacity 0)
style_en: Illustration Line Illustration Stroke by Stroke Drawing Hand-drawn Diagram Line Art Illustration Draw Sketch

desc_en: Hovering over a line icon redraws its strokes and lifts it slightly
prompt_en: A row of line icons (home, search, heart, notifications), each placed inside a rounded-corner square frame; when the mouse moves over an icon, that icon's lines are redrawn from the beginning (about 0.7 seconds, multiple strokes staggered by 0.12 seconds), the frame border and the lines simultaneously switch to the accent color, and the icon lifts slightly by 6px and returns. (GSAP: on pointerenter, for that icon's path / circle elements, fromTo drawSVG "0%"→"100%", with overwrite:true to avoid conflicts when hovering across quickly)
style_en: Icon icon Line Icon hover Redraw Stroke Menu Navigation Icon Stroke Draw Hover Menu

desc_en: Dashed connectors between nodes keep flowing, with small dots traveling along the lines
prompt_en: In a flowchart or system architecture diagram, the nodes (circles + labels underneath) are connected with smooth curves; the connectors are dashed lines whose dashes keep moving in the direction of the data flow, and small dots also travel back and forth along each connector, expressing that data is flowing; the speed is steady and loops without stopping. (CSS: set stroke-dasharray on the paths and use keyframes to continuously change stroke-dashoffset; the small dots use SVG animateMotion or CSS offset-path to move along the same path, each with an offset start time)
style_en: Flowchart Architecture Diagram Node Connector Dashed Line Flow Data Flow Flow Diagram Connector Dashed Line Data Flow

desc_en: Multiple wave layers at the bottom of a section flow slowly at different speeds
prompt_en: A wave shape separates two sections. The wave is made of 3 layers — the back layer paler and taller, the front layer more solid and lower — and the three layers flow slowly left and right at different speeds (about 6, 9, and 13 seconds per cycle), in not entirely the same direction, creating a sense of depth like water, looping seamlessly. (CSS: each layer is an SVG path 200% wide containing two full wavelengths, using a linear infinite animation of translateX(0 → -50%) for seamlessness; different layers are given different animation-duration and direction)
style_en: Wave Divider Section Separator Water Wave Ocean Wave Wave Divider Section Separator Liquid

desc_en: A ring draws to a specified percentage while the number in the middle counts up in sync
prompt_en: A circular progress chart, with a low-contrast track ring underneath. On entry, the progress arc starts at the very top and draws clockwise to a specified percentage (for example 78%), with a rounded line cap; the percentage number in the middle counts up in sync from 0 to 78%, with small text underneath labeling the item's name; about 1.8 seconds, ease-in-out, stopping at the result. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin drawSVG "0%"→"0% 78%", the SVG as a whole rotate(-90deg) so the start point is at the top; the number tweens an object value + onUpdate to write it in, with the same timing and ease as the arc)
style_en: Progress Ring Percentage Gauge Data Statistics Progress Ring Donut Percentage Gauge Stats

desc_en: A circle is drawn first, then a checkmark pops, and finally a success message appears
prompt_en: The success state after submitting or completing payment: first a circle is drawn (about 0.8 seconds), then a checkmark is quickly drawn inside the circle (about 0.45 seconds); the instant the check finishes, the whole icon pops slightly bigger by 8% and back, while the 'Payment Successful' text below fades in from 8px below. Clean, clear, and reassuring. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin draws the circle and the check path in sequence; the icon scale 1→1.08 yoyo; the text fromTo y:8 / opacity:0)
style_en: Success Complete Checkmark Tick Confirm Submit Payment State Success Check Done Confirm Tick

desc_en: As the round knob slides to the other side it stretches slightly, and the track switches state along with it
prompt_en: A toggle switch on an app settings page: when clicked, the round knob slides from one side to the other; during the slide, the knob first stretches horizontally and then shrinks back (like elastic jelly), overshooting slightly on arrival before settling into place; the track simultaneously switches to the accent color of the on state, and returns to a low-contrast state when off. About 0.35 seconds. (CSS: a button with role="switch"; the knob uses a left transition with cubic-bezier(.5,1.4,.5,1) for the overshoot, plus keyframes that widen it at 50%; remember to update aria-checked)
style_en: Toggle Switch switch toggle Settings iOS Round Knob App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: Pull a list down, a spinning icon appears, and on release it loads and springs back
prompt_en: When you pull down at the top of a mobile list page, the list follows the finger downward (the further you pull, the greater the resistance), and a circular loading icon is revealed above; the icon's rotation angle increases with the pull distance. On release, the icon keeps spinning to indicate loading; when loading finishes, the list smoothly springs back to the top, and the newest item is briefly highlighted before fading back. (GSAP: get the pull distance from the gesture using Draggable or Observer and multiply it by a damping coefficient; on release, a timeline: spinner rotation → list y back to 0 (power3.out) → the new item's background fades out)
style_en: Pull Down Refresh Reload List Gesture Pull Refresh Spinner Gesture App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: The background dims and a menu slides up from the bottom with a little spring
prompt_en: After tapping an action such as 'Share,' the screen gets a translucent overlay that gradually darkens, and a menu panel slides up from the bottom of the screen with a slight bounce (about 0.6 seconds). The panel has a small handle at its top, and the options inside fade in in sequence from 8px below; on close, the panel slides quickly down and out (about 0.35 seconds, accelerating) and the overlay fades out. (GSAP: panel yPercent 100→0, ease back.out(1.1); options stagger 0.06; closing uses power2.in; in a real app, the user can drag the handle down to close it)
style_en: Bottom Sheet Bottom Menu Popup Share Action Menu Bottom Sheet Action Sheet Drawer Modal App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: When a tab is tapped, the pill indicator stretches and slides to the new position, and the icon pops
prompt_en: An app's pill-shaped bottom navigation bar has 4 icons, with a pill indicator under the current tab; when another tab is tapped, the indicator first stretches toward the target, covering both the old and new positions at once (about 0.18 seconds), then contracts onto the new tab (about 0.34 seconds, decelerating), flowing across like liquid; the new tab's icon simultaneously pops back from 0.7x to its original size, contrasting with the indicator. (GSAP: a two-stage timeline changes the indicator's x and width; the icon scale uses back.out(3))
style_en: Bottom Navigation Bar Tabs tab bar Navigation Indicator Switch Bottom Navigation Indicator Gooey App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: Swiping a list item left reveals delete; swiping all the way collapses and removes it
prompt_en: List items can be swiped left with a finger, revealing a warning-colored 'Delete' button behind the item; if released with less than half the distance swiped, it springs back into place; if released past the threshold (about 30%), the item slides entirely off the screen to the left, then that row's height collapses to 0 and the items below smoothly move up to fill in. (GSAP: Draggable type:"x", restricted to leftward only, edgeResistance 0.8; onRelease, judge the threshold, then xPercent:-100, then tween height to 0; on mobile, set touch-action:pan-y so vertical scrolling is not affected)
style_en: Swipe Delete Swipe Left List Gesture Collapse Swipe Delete Gesture List Dismiss App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction
txt_en: Meeting Reminder Billing Notice New Message

desc_en: On press, the button shrinks into a spinning circle, then a checkmark appears on completion and it restores
prompt_en: When the 'Submit' button is clicked, the button first presses in gently (scaling to 95%), the text fades out, and the button's width contracts into a circle (about 0.4 seconds) with a spinning loading ring appearing inside it; when done, the loading ring disappears and is replaced by a checkmark being drawn, and the button pops slightly; after holding for about 0.8 seconds, it expands back to its original width and the text fades in. This prevents duplicate clicks and lets the user clearly know the state. (GSAP: a timeline tweens in sequence the width, the spinner rotation, and the DrawSVG checkmark; the width uses fromTo with fixed units)
style_en: Button Loading Submit Spinner Success Checkmark State Loading Button Submit Spinner Success Morph App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: Tapping plus or minus gives button feedback, and the number rolls up or down to switch
prompt_en: A quantity selector for a shopping cart: minus and plus round buttons on the left and right, and a number in the middle; when a button is pressed, the button shrinks and switches to the accent color as feedback, and the number scrolls to switch according to direction — when increasing, the old number slides out upward and the new number slides in from below; when decreasing, the direction is reversed — about 0.3 seconds; at the upper and lower limits, the number no longer changes. (CSS: the number container has overflow:hidden; the old and new numbers each use keyframes with translateY ±100% to enter and exit, and the old element is removed when finished)
style_en: Quantity Plus Minus Stepper Cart Count Stepper Counter Quantity Plus Minus Cart App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: When you tap into an input, the hint text shrinks and floats up, and the underline expands from the center
prompt_en: A form input normally shows only a hint label like a placeholder; when you tap in (focus), the label shrinks and floats up above the input, while the underline expands from the center out to both sides in the accent color and the cursor starts blinking; after entering content and leaving, the label stays in the small-text state above, returning to its original position only when the field is cleared. About 0.3–0.4 seconds, decelerating. (CSS: the label is absolutely positioned, using :focus-within or :not(:placeholder-shown) to change top and font-size; the underline uses transform:scaleX(0→1))
style_en: Input Form Label Floating Focus Floating Label Input Focus Form Material App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: When a rating is selected, the stars light up in sequence from left to right and pop
prompt_en: Five hollow stars: when the user taps star N, stars 1 through N fill in from left to right in sequence and each pops larger from small (about 0.08 seconds between each), while the rest stay hollow; matching text feedback appears below in sync (for example 'Very good' or 'Amazing!'). When fewer stars are selected, the extra stars turn hollow again. (CSS: toggle .on for the fill color and .pop for the pop keyframes, staggered by index using setTimeout or transition-delay; each star is a button with an aria-label)
style_en: Rating Stars Review Feedback Rating Stars Review Feedback App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: The launch logo pops out and breathes, then zooms through the screen into the home page
prompt_en: When the app opens, the logo in the center of the screen pops out from small (back.out) and breathes gently once; then the logo accelerates and zooms until it fills the whole screen and fades out, as if passing through the logo into the app, while the home content underneath (hero card, list) fades in and rises in sequence from top to bottom. The whole sequence is about 2 seconds, ending on the home screen. (GSAP: timeline: logo scale 0.6→1 → yoyo 1.06 → scale 14 (power3.in) + the splash layer opacity 0 → home elements stagger fromTo y:10 / opacity:0)
style_en: Splash Screen Opening splash Loading Logo Home Transition Launch Screen Intro Zoom Through App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: On an input error, the field shakes left and right and an error message slides out below
prompt_en: When the password is wrong at login, the input field shakes rapidly left and right a few times (like shaking its head no, about 0.45 seconds, with the amplitude growing then shrinking), the border simultaneously switches to the error color, and the error message below fades and slides in from 4px above; after the input is corrected, the border and message return to normal. (CSS: keyframes use translateX to move left and right across 10%–90%, cubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97); before replaying, remove the class and trigger a reflow; it can be paired with phone vibration via navigator.vibrate)
