style_en: Error Shake Shaking Validation Password Login Form Shake Error Validation Wrong Password Login App Mobile Mobile Device Micro-interaction Mobile App Micro-interaction

desc_en: The characters of a paragraph brighten one by one from faint as you scroll
prompt_en: A passage in large type is fixed at the center of the screen, with all characters very faint at first; as the user scrolls down, the characters become clear in sequence starting from the first one — scroll progress equals the proportion lit — and scrolling back dims them in sequence again, like copy presentation on Apple's official site. (GSAP: SplitText splits the characters, fromTo opacity 0.15→1, stagger 0.1, ease none, bound to ScrollTrigger scrub:true; the section is fixed with pin or position:sticky, and the outer height is about 3–4 viewports)
style_en: Character by Character Light Up Paragraph Copy Apple Official Site Text Reveal Highlight On Scroll Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered
txt_en: Great motion design lights up word by word as you scroll, guiding your eyes down through this sentence.

desc_en: A small image zooms with scrolling until it fills the screen, then a heading appears
prompt_en: A small image with rounded corners at the center of the screen (about 40% wide) gradually enlarges as you scroll down until it fills the whole screen; its corners simultaneously shrink to square corners, and the image content slowly scales back from 1.3x to its original size (so it does not look blurry when enlarged); late in the enlargement, a heading fades in from below, overlaid on the image; scrolling back reverses everything. (GSAP: a timeline bound to ScrollTrigger scrub:true, with the section pinned or sticky; tween width / height / borderRadius and the inner layer's scale; clip-path inset can also be used)
style_en: Image Zoom Full-bleed Full Screen Expand Zoom Image Expand Full Screen Fullbleed Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: Cards scroll up one by one and stack over each other, while the one below shrinks and darkens
prompt_en: A set of large cards arranged in sequence; when each card scrolls to near the top of the screen it sticks (each card's resting position is offset slightly further down, so the edge of the previous card is visible); when the next card scrolls up and stacks on top of it, the covered card simultaneously shrinks to about 90% and darkens, creating the depth of a stack of cards; scrolling back restores it. (CSS position:sticky + top increasing by index; with GSAP, each card gets a ScrollTrigger that scrubs its scale and brightness over the range 'from the next card entering the viewport to its reaching the top')
style_en: Cards Stacking Sticky sticky Stacked Service Intro Stacking Cards Sticky Stack Deck Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: Numbers only start counting up from zero when the data section scrolls into view
prompt_en: A results-data section in the middle of the page (three cells: a number + a label). When scrolled to the point where the data section is about 80% into the viewport, the three cells fade in from below in sequence while the numbers count up from 0 to their target values at the same time (for example 128, 99%, 4.9, decimals allowed), about 1.6 seconds, decelerating; scrolling back up out of view resets it, so it plays again the next time it is scrolled to (or plays only once). (GSAP: ScrollTrigger.create { start:"top 80%", onEnter, onLeaveBack }; the number tweens an object value + onUpdate, using toFixed to control the number of decimal places)
style_en: Data Statistics Count Numbers Results KPI Count Up Stats Numbers On Scroll Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered
txt_en: Projects Completed Client Satisfaction Average Rating

desc_en: The navigation bar hides when scrolling down and slides out immediately when scrolling back up
prompt_en: The header navigation bar is fixed at the top; when the user scrolls down (reading content), the navigation bar slides up out of the screen to make room; as soon as they scroll up (looking for the menu), it immediately slides back in from the top, and it is always shown at the very top; about 0.35 seconds, decelerating. Very common on mobile. (How to: compare the current and previous scrollY to judge direction, or use ScrollTrigger's self.direction; toggle a class so the header uses translateY(-100%), with a transition)
style_en: Navigation Bar Header Menu header navbar Hide Show Direction Headroom Hide On Scroll Down Show On Scroll Up Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: A curve draws its way down with scrolling, connecting each section
prompt_en: In the page background there is a curve winding left and right through the whole stretch of content, with a very faint track underneath it first; as you scroll down, the accent-colored line draws along the track, drawing as far as you have scrolled, and retracts when you scroll back; several nodes along the line (dots + headings) fade in alternately from both sides as the line approaches. Suited to brand stories, journeys, and history introductions. (GSAP: DrawSVGPlugin drawSVG 0%→100% bound to ScrollTrigger scrub; the SVG is the same height as the content, preserveAspectRatio:none; each node fades in with its own toggleActions)
style_en: Path Curve Line Drawing Timeline Journey Story Scroll Path Draw SVG Line Journey Story Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: An image moves inside its frame more slowly than the scroll, creating depth
prompt_en: A column of images arranged top to bottom, each image in a fixed frame that crops the overflow, with the image itself somewhat taller than the frame; when scrolling, the image displaces in reverse inside the frame at a slower speed (from about +12% to −12%), looking like scenery outside a window and giving more depth than scrolling as one whole block; there is a short caption below each image. (GSAP: the frame has overflow:hidden, the inner image is about 128% tall; each image gets its own ScrollTrigger, start "top bottom", end "bottom top", scrubbing yPercent -12→12)
style_en: Image Parallax Frame Photo Depth Image Parallax Frame Inner Parallax Gallery Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: Three lines of large text move left and right in opposite directions with scrolling, the middle one hollow
prompt_en: There are three lines of extra-large repeated text on screen (the middle line is hollow outline), and when scrolling, the first and third lines move left while the second line moves right, with the distance moved entirely following scroll progress (stopping when scrolling stops), creating a tense layout rhythm. (GSAP: a timeline bound to ScrollTrigger scrub:0.6, each line fromTo xPercent 0↔-40; the section is pinned or sticky)
style_en: Big Type Horizontal Shift Marquee Reverse Heading Scroll Marquee Big Type Horizontal Text Kinetic Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: When scrolled to different sections, the whole page's background and text scheme switch along with it
prompt_en: The page is divided into several sections, each with its own background and text color theme; when a section scrolls to the middle line of the screen, the whole page's background and text smoothly transition over about 0.6 seconds to that section's theme, and scrolling back switches back to the previous one, so each chapter has a clear mood change. (GSAP: one ScrollTrigger per section, start "top 50%", end "bottom 50%", switching CSS variables or a class onToggle; CSS adds a transition to background / color)
style_en: Background Theme Switch Section Block Section Theme Background Change On Scroll Chapters Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: When scrolling, a circular mask expands from the center, revealing the next chapter
prompt_en: A transition between two sections: when scrolling, the next section appears from the center of the screen through a circular mask; the circle expands with scroll progress from 0 until it covers the whole screen, while the previous section's heading slowly shrinks and fades and the next section's heading scales back from 1.2x to its original size; scrolling back shrinks the circle back. (GSAP: a timeline bound to ScrollTrigger scrub, with the section pinned or sticky; tween clipPath "circle(0% at 50% 50%)" → "circle(75% at 50% 50%)")
style_en: Transition Circle Mask Expand Reveal Section Circle Reveal Clip Path Transition Section Scroll Scroll scroll ScrollTrigger scrub Scroll-triggered

desc_en: Hovering over a link grows an underline from the left, and leaving retracts it to the right
prompt_en: Text links in a navigation bar: when the mouse moves in, a thin underline grows from left to right; when the mouse moves out, the underline continues retracting to the right (instead of shrinking back the way it came), like a sweep of light passing through; about 0.45 seconds, ease-in-out. (CSS: ::after makes the underline, transform:scaleX(0); on hover, scaleX(1) with transform-origin:left; when not hovering, transform-origin:right, transition cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1))

desc_en: Hovering over hollow large text fills it solid from left to right
prompt_en: A few lines of extra-large hollow outline text: when the mouse moves over a line, that line fills in to solid from left to right (like ink pouring in), and when the mouse moves away, it retreats back to hollow from right to left; about 0.6 seconds, ease-in-out, suited to portfolio headings or menus. (CSS: the text uses -webkit-text-stroke for the outline, color:transparent; the background uses a solid-color linear-gradient with background-clip:text, and on hover, background-size 0%→100% with a transition)
style_en: Hollow Text Outline Fill Big Type outline stroke text fill hover hover Hover Mouse Enter Hover Interaction

desc_en: Hovering over a card flips it in 3D to its back, showing more information
prompt_en: A row of project cards, with the hero visual and heading on the front; when the mouse moves in, the card flips 180 degrees in 3D around the vertical axis to the back, which shows action text such as 'View Project →', with a slight overshoot bounce to the flip; moving out flips it back to the front. About 0.7 seconds. (CSS: the outer layer has perspective, the inner layer transform-style:preserve-3d + a transition on transform, rotateY(180deg) on hover; both faces have backface-visibility:hidden, and the back face is pre-rotated rotateY(180deg))
style_en: Card Flip Turnover Front and Back 3D flip card hover Back Side Hover Mouse Enter Hover Interaction

desc_en: A circular thumbnail expands on hover into a tall rounded card and a title fades in
prompt_en: A row of circular image thumbnails. When the mouse moves over one, the circle smoothly becomes a taller portrait rounded rectangle (growing downward at the same time), the image content scales back from 1.18x to its original size, revealing more of the picture, and the title below fades in; moving away restores the circle. About 0.55 seconds, ease-out. Suitable for team members or work categories. (CSS: outer frame border-radius 50% to a small rounded corner, height transitions in sync; inner image transform: scale 1.18 to 1; title opacity / translateY)
style_en: image circle expand thumbnail avatar team image shape expand circle hover hover hover mouse-enter hover-over interaction

desc_en: As the cursor sweeps over a row of icons, nearby icons magnify and push their neighbors aside
prompt_en: A row of rounded icons like the macOS Dock: when the cursor moves left and right near the icon row, the icon closest to the cursor magnifies to about 1.9x, and the neighboring icons to its left and right magnify in decreasing amounts according to distance, forming a smooth magnification peak and pushing the other icons aside to both sides; when the cursor leaves, all return to their original size. (How to: on mousemove, calculate the horizontal distance between each icon's center and the cursor, scale = 1 + 0.9 × max(0, 1 − distance/influence range), write it into CSS variables controlling width / height so the layout naturally pushes apart; add a short transition to make the change smooth)
style_en: Dock magnify icons menu macOS toolbar magnify icons toolbar hover hover mouse-enter hover-over interaction

desc_en: When you hover over a menu item, a background pill slider follows to that item
prompt_en: A pill-shaped navigation bar. When the mouse moves over an item, a pill background slider smoothly slides over from its original position and changes width to fit that item, and the text simultaneously switches to a color that contrasts with the slider; when the mouse leaves the whole menu, the slider returns to the item for the current page. About 0.4 seconds, with a slight overshoot. (How to: on pointerenter, read the item's offsetLeft and offsetWidth, set the slider's translateX and width, transition cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1.1))
style_en: menu navigation slider pill highlight follow nav pill hover indicator tabs hover hover mouse-enter hover-over interaction

desc_en: A row of narrow image panels; the hovered panel expands wider and shows its title
prompt_en: A row of equally wide vertical-strip image panels. When the mouse moves over one panel, it smoothly expands to about 4 times the width of the others, the other panels narrow in sync, and after the expansion completes the title at the bottom-left of that panel fades in; moving to another panel hands off smoothly. About 0.6 seconds, ease-out. Suitable for work categories or gallery entrances. (CSS: container display:flex, each panel flex:1, on hover flex:4, transition flex; images use object-fit:cover to avoid distortion; title gets a transition-delay)
style_en: image panel expand accordion album gallery accordion expanding panels flex hover hover mouse-enter hover-over interaction
txt_en: Mountains Flowers Night Sky Sunset Coast

desc_en: When you hover over an icon, a tooltip pops up elastically from below
prompt_en: A row of circular icon buttons. When the mouse moves over an icon, a tooltip with a small triangular arrow pops up above it, elastically scaling up from about 60% size and a slightly lower position, using the arrow as the origin, and moving up into place (about 0.3 seconds, with a slight overshoot); moving away fades it out and shrinks it back. (CSS: tooltip position:absolute, transform-origin set at the arrow, on hover scale(0.6) to 1 + translateY + opacity, transition cubic-bezier(.3,1.5,.5,1); remember pointer-events:none to avoid flickering)
style_en: tooltip tooltip explanation hint bubble popover hover hint hover hover mouse-enter hover-over interaction

desc_en: When you glide over text, each letter you touch bounces once on its own
prompt_en: Title text is split into individual characters. Whichever character the cursor glides over, that character bounces up once and briefly turns into an accent color (about 0.5 seconds, elastic), and a fast horizontal sweep of the cursor forms a wave in succession; each character's animation is independent, and it returns to its original position when finished. (How to: wrap each character in an inline-block span, on pointerenter remove and re-add the animation class to replay it, remove it on animationend; keyframes at 30% translateY(-35%) scale(1.12))

desc_en: When you hover over a button, its four borders are drawn in sequence to enclose it
prompt_en: A button with only a very faint thin frame normally. On mouse-enter, an accent-colored border is drawn in sequence starting from the top-left corner: top edge to the right, then right edge downward, then bottom edge to the left, then left edge upward, each segment about 0.18 seconds, joining up to enclose the button, and when the drawing finishes the text also changes to the accent color; on mouse-leave it retracts in the reverse order. (CSS: four absolutely positioned line elements, each using scaleX / scaleY with a different transform-origin; use transition-delay to arrange the order, with opposite delays for the hover and non-hover states)

desc_en: Stars fly outward from the center into streaks of light; hovering speeds them up
prompt_en: The Hero background is a field of stars flying toward the camera: each star starts near the center of the screen, gets brighter and larger as it approaches the viewer, and pulls out short radial streaks of light, like a spaceship accelerating through space; when the cursor moves into the section, the speed smoothly increases, and the vanishing point shifts slightly toward the cursor direction, returning slowly to cruising speed after it leaves. The foreground title stays clear. (Canvas 2D: each star has x, y, z, z decreases each frame, projected coordinates = center + x/z × focal length, draw a line from the previous frame's projected position to this frame's; cover the screen with a translucent background color to create afterimages)

desc_en: Hundreds of fine lines flow slowly along an invisible current; the cursor stirs the flow
prompt_en: The background is filled with hundreds of invisible small particles. Each particle advances according to the 'flow direction' at its location (determined by smoothly varying noise or trigonometric functions, and changing slowly over time) and leaves a very fine trail. The trails fade out gradually, and the whole flows continuously like patterns of wind or water; the flow direction near the cursor is twisted, forming a stirred vortex. (Canvas 2D: each frame first cover the screen with a low-opacity background color to create trails, then let each particle advance a small step according to angle = f(x, y, t) and draw a line; particles respawn when their lifespan ends or they go out of bounds; simplex noise can be used to make the flow field more natural)
style_en: flow field current lines generative art organic Flow Field Generative Art Perlin Noise Lines Canvas particles particles requestAnimationFrame interactive background

desc_en: Petals drift down slowly while rotating; the cursor passing by blows them away
prompt_en: Dozens of petals drift slowly down from the top of the background. Each sways side to side, flips over (simulating a flip with scaling) and rotates individually, with slightly different speeds and sizes; when the cursor passes by, it blows nearby petals away according to its movement direction and speed, after which the petals slowly return to their natural falling. It can also be swapped for weather particles such as snowflakes or raindrops. style_en: Price Plans Subscription Monthly Yearly Pricing Table Pricing Table Plans Toggle Monthly Yearly SaaS Cards Group

desc_en: Clicking a card smoothly enlarges it into a detail panel while the other cards fade out
prompt_en: A row of work cards; when one is clicked, it smoothly enlarges from its original position and size into a detail panel that fills the whole area (large image on the left, title and description on the right), while the other cards fade out at the same time; the text inside the detail fades in in sequence around the completion of the enlargement; clicking again shrinks it back to its original position and the other cards fade back in. About 0.6 seconds, ease-in-out. (GSAP Flip: use Flip.getState to record all cards, then toggle the enlarged card's class (changing it to absolute positioning that fills the container with a new layout), then Flip.from to tween, with nested:true so inner elements transform along with it)
style_en: Cards Expand Details Enlarge Shared Element shared element transition Expand Detail Flip Cards Group

desc_en: Two rows of cards move infinitely in opposite directions, and pause when the mouse moves over them
prompt_en: Two rows of testimonial or client cards move horizontally in an infinite loop, the top row to the left and the bottom row to the right, at a slow, steady speed; when the mouse moves over the card wall both rows pause for easy reading, and continue when it moves away. Suitable for client testimonials and partner logo walls. (CSS: each row's content is duplicated twice on the same track, and keyframes translateX(0 to -50%) linear infinite achieves a seamless loop; the reverse row uses animation-direction:reverse; on :hover, animation-play-state:paused)
style_en: Marquee Card Wall Testimonials Clients Logo Wall Infinite Infinite Marquee Testimonials Logo Wall Cards Group

desc_en: The quote fades out and moves up to switch to the next one, avatars switch along with it, and a progress bar keeps time
prompt_en: A client testimonial carousel: in the center is a large quote and attribution, with a row of circular avatars and a progress bar below; about every 2.6 seconds, the current quote fades out upward and the next one fades in and slides up from below, the corresponding avatar enlarges and gains a ring while the other avatars shrink and fade, and the progress bar restarts filling from 0 to keep time; clicking an avatar switches directly to that testimonial. (GSAP: tween the y and opacity of the old and new quotes separately; the progress bar goes scaleX 0 to 1 with ease none, with a duration equal to the auto-switch interval)
style_en: Testimonials Recommendations Client Testimonials Carousel Quote Testimonial Review Quote Slider Carousel Cards Group
txt_en: Ms. Wang Mr. Chen Designer Lin

desc_en: Masonry cards of varying heights fall into place row by row with a slight rotation
prompt_en: A Masonry gallery entrance: cards in three columns of varying heights, in reading order from top to bottom and left to right, fall one by one from about 30px above with a slight random rotation and fade in, with a slight rebound as they settle (interval about 0.09 seconds), so the whole gallery looks as if it is being placed piece by piece. (GSAP: after sorting by each card's row and column index, stagger 0.09, fromTo y:-30 / opacity:0 / rotation:random(-6,6) back to zero, ease back.out(1.4); on a real site, layout can be done with CSS columns or a masonry library)
style_en: Masonry masonry Pinterest Gallery Entrance Fall Masonry Grid Cascade Gallery Cards Group

desc_en: When hovering over a card it lifts up, while the other cards fade and shrink
prompt_en: A row of cards; when the mouse moves over one card, it lifts slightly and enlarges to 1.04x, while the other cards simultaneously fade, blur slightly, desaturate and shrink to 95%, focusing attention on the current card; when the mouse leaves the whole row, everything returns to normal. About 0.45 seconds, decelerating. (CSS: when the container is :hover, .card:not(:hover) gets reduced opacity, filter:blur(1px) saturate(.6) and scale(.95); the hovered card gets translateY + scale; :has() can be used to support keyboard focus)
style_en: Focus Dim Other Cards hover Highlight Focus Dim Siblings Highlight Spotlight Cards Group

desc_en: Click add to cart, and the product thumbnail flies in an arc into the cart while the count jumps
prompt_en: When the "Add to Cart" button on a product card is pressed, the button gives a light press feedback, a copy of the product thumbnail flies along a parabolic arc to the cart icon at the top right, gradually shrinking during flight; on arrival the cart bounces and enlarges once, and the count badge in the corner increments by 1 and pops out. About 0.75 seconds, giving the user clear "added" feedback. (GSAP: tween the flying element's x with power1.in and y with back.in separately to form an arc, while scaling from 1 to 0.15; on completion remove the element and update the badge, with the badge scale using back.out(3))
style_en: Cart Add E-commerce Fly In Parabola Feedback Add To Cart Fly Ecommerce Shop Feedback Cards Group

desc_en: A soft, large gradient flows slowly, with a layer of fine, flickering film grain on top
prompt_en: A Hero background of three large, soft-edged gradient glows that slowly move in an interlaced pattern and drift back and forth on a cycle of about 12 seconds; on top is a layer of very fine film grain (noise) texture, with the grain flickering several times per second, giving the image an analog print-like texture, while the foreground title stays clear. (CSS: multiple radial-gradients layered in the same background, with keyframes animating background-position; the grain layer uses noise generated by SVG feTurbulence as its background-image, with mix-blend-mode:overlay and low opacity, using steps() keyframes with random displacement to create the flicker)
style_en: Grain Noise Film Grain Gradient Texture Grain Noise Film Gradient Texture Mesh Gradient mesh gradient Background Atmosphere

desc_en: A striped sunset above the horizon, and a perspective grid floor continuously advancing forward
prompt_en: An 80s synthwave-style background: in the middle of the screen is a horizon line; above it is a circular sunset whose lower half is cut by horizontal stripes, with a soft glow; below is a perspective-tilted grid floor whose grid lines continuously advance toward the viewer and fade out in the distance, creating a feeling of endlessly driving forward; the title floats above the sunset with a slight glow. (CSS: the floor is two sets of linear-gradient grid lines, with transform:perspective + rotateX(72deg), and keyframes advancing background-position by one grid length for a seamless loop; the far end fades out with a mask; the sunset stripes use a repeating-linear-gradient mask)
style_en: Retro Synthwave synthwave vaporwave Perspective Grid Floor Horizon Sunset 80s Retro Grid Horizon Perspective Background Atmosphere

desc_en: Soft-focus light spots of different sizes slowly float upward, fading in and out
prompt_en: In the background float more than ten circular light spots of different sizes with a soft-focus blur; each slowly floats upward from below at a different speed (about 7-14 seconds), drifting slightly left and right along the way, fading in as it appears and fading out near the top, each with different opacity, creating a dreamy, warm atmosphere; the title in the center stays clear. (CSS: each light spot uses CSS variables to set its size, horizontal position, duration, negative animation-delay and offset, with filter:blur, and keyframes control translate and opacity)
style_en: Bokeh Light Spots Soft Focus Bubbles Floating Rise Dreamy Bokeh Lights Bubbles Floating Blur Background Atmosphere

desc_en: A center point pulses regularly, and rings expand outward one after another and fade out
prompt_en: At the center of the screen is a solid dot that gently pulses regularly; from its position, thin rings continuously expand outward one after another, growing larger and gradually fading away, with multiple rings offset in time to form continuous ripples, like radar, sound waves, or a "live" signal; a short label can be placed on the center dot. (CSS: 3-4 rings share the same keyframes: scale 0.15 to 1.25, opacity 0.9 to 0, evenly offset with negative animation-delay; the center dot uses another scale keyframes)
style_en: Concentric Circles Expand Pulse Radar Sound Waves Live Location Signal Pulse Rings Ripple Radar Signal Live Background Atmosphere

desc_en: Radial rays slowly rotate behind the title, brightest at the center and fading outward
prompt_en: Behind the title is a ring of ray stripes radiating outward from the center; the whole ring slowly rotates at a speed of about 30 seconds per revolution, brightest at the center and gradually blending into the background outward, like the spotlight effect of an award, prize draw, or celebration scene. (CSS: repeating-conic-gradient draws the radial stripes and is enlarged beyond the container, keyframes rotate 360deg linear infinite; a radial-gradient layer on top makes the center bright and the edges dark)
style_en: Rays Radiate Sunlight Rotating Celebration Award Prize Draw Sunburst Rays Rotating God Rays Conic Background Atmosphere

desc_en: Stars all over the sky twinkle individually, a meteor occasionally streaks past, and the starry sky shifts with slight parallax as the cursor moves
prompt_en: A night-sky background: darker at the top with a soft glow lower down, filled with more than two hundred stars of different sizes and brightness, each twinkling slowly at its own speed and phase; when the brightest few reach peak brightness, fine cross-shaped sparkles appear; every few seconds a meteor streaks from the upper right diagonally down to the lower left, trailing a fading tail; when the cursor moves, the starry sky makes reverse parallax shifts of different magnitudes depending on the stars' depths. (Canvas 2D: each star records its position, radius, depth, twinkle frequency and phase, with brightness = sin(time x frequency + phase); meteors are line segments drawn with createLinearGradient; parallax displacement is smoothed with lerp)
style_en: Starry Sky Stars Twinkle Meteor Night Sky Universe Parallax Twinkling Stars Night Sky Shooting Star Canvas particles requestAnimationFrame Interactive Background Background Atmosphere

desc_en: Three layers of graphics, front, middle and back, move in reverse following the cursor at different magnitudes according to distance, creating a sense of depth
prompt_en: A Hero background made of three layers of decorative graphics: the far layer is a blurred large circle, the middle layer is a rounded square, and the front layer is a hollow ring, with the title sandwiched between the middle and front layers; when the cursor moves inside the section, each layer moves in the opposite direction from the cursor, with layers closer to the viewer moving more (for example far layer 15%, middle layer 45%, front layer 100%), and the title moves only slightly, creating a three-dimensional sense of depth, with smooth delayed following in the movement. (JS: mousemove calculates the cursor's ratio relative to the center, -0.5 to 0.5; each layer's translate = -ratio x that layer's coefficient, smoothed with a CSS transition or lerp)
style_en: Parallax Depth Layers Three-Dimensional Mouse Cursor Mouse Parallax Depth Layers 3D Hero Background Atmosphere

desc_en: A whole field of fine lines undulates like fabric, and the places the cursor passes are gently arched up
prompt_en: The entire background is about 26 horizontal fine lines, each undulating from the superposition of two sets of sine waves of different frequencies and flowing slowly over time, with adjacent lines slightly offset in phase, so the whole field looks like flowing fabric or terrain lines; among them, every few lines are accented with a thicker, brighter line; where the cursor passes, nearby lines are smoothly arched upward, and recover after it leaves. (Canvas 2D: each line takes 80 points, y = baseline + sin(x*f1 + t + j*phase) * A1 + sin(x*f2 - t + j*phase) * A2, minus a Gaussian function centered on the cursor times height)
style_en: Lines Waves Undulate Fabric Terrain Contour Lines Wavy Lines Wave Field Terrain Canvas Interactive Background requestAnimationFrame Background Atmosphere

desc_en: Geometric shapes such as circles, squares, triangles and rings randomly float and rotate slowly in the background
prompt_en: More than ten simple geometric shapes are scattered in the background: solid circles, rounded squares, triangles, hollow rings and crosses, of different sizes; on entrance each appears in sequence with an elastic scale-up, after which each shape continuously drifts slowly in a random direction and rotates, choosing a new random target on each round trip, looking natural and non-repetitive; the title sits in the middle. (GSAP: for each shape, gsap.to on x / y / rotation uses "random(-40,40)" strings, with duration random(3,6), ease sine.inOut, repeat:-1, yoyo:true, repeatRefresh:true; entrance with gsap.from scale:0 paired with back.out)
style_en: Floating Geometric Shapes Random Decoration Background Floating Shapes Geometric Random Decoration Background Atmosphere

desc_en: There is a layer of thickness beneath the button; when pressed, the whole button presses down and the thickness disappears, like a physical key
prompt_en: A button with the feel of a physical key: below the button body is a layer of "thickness" in the same color family but darker (made with an unblurred shadow below), with another layer of soft shadow around the outside; when the mouse hovers, the button lifts slightly and the thickness increases; when pressed, the whole button presses down until almost flat, the thickness and shadow shrink, and it springs back on release. About 0.12 seconds, crisp and responsive. (CSS: box-shadow: 0 6px 0 darker color, 0 10px 20px semi-transparent; on :active, translateY(5px) and shrink the first shadow layer to 1px)
style_en: Three-Dimensional Press Physical Key 3D Pressable Button Push Tactile Game Button

desc_en: On hover or click, the button is squashed flat like jelly, stretched long, then bounces back
prompt_en: When the mouse hovers over or clicks it, the button, like jelly, is first squashed horizontally flat (width 1.18, height 0.82), then stretched vertically long (width 0.85, height 1.15), then wobbles back and forth a few times with decreasing amplitude until it returns to its original shape; the whole sequence is about 0.7 seconds, bouncy and cute. (CSS keyframes: in sequence scale(1.18,.82) then (.85,1.15) then (1.08,.92) then (.97,1.03) then (1,1); when triggered by a click, first remove the class, force a reflow, then add it back so it can replay)
style_en: Jelly Bounce Bouncy Squash Stretch Jelly Rubber Squash Stretch Bounce Button Button

desc_en: A ripple spreads out from the exact position the finger taps, the classic Material Design feedback
prompt_en: When the button is clicked, a circular ripple spreads out from the exact point the finger (cursor) pressed, semi-transparent, growing from small to large enough to cover the whole button while fading out at the same time, about 0.7 seconds; consecutive clicks can produce multiple ripples at once. (JS: on pointerdown, calculate the click position and the distance to the farthest corner x 2 as the diameter, insert a circular span, CSS keyframes scale 0 to 1 with opacity fading, and remove it on animationend; the button has overflow:hidden)
style_en: Ripple Water Wave Click Feedback Material Design Ripple Click Feedback Ink Button

desc_en: Drag the round knob all the way to the end to confirm; if it does not reach the end it springs back, and the text has a shimmer hint
prompt_en: A capsule-shaped slide track, with a round handle on the left (with a right arrow inside), and a beam of light sweeps across the hint text in the middle from left to right; when the user drags the handle, the track the handle has passed is filled and the hint text gradually fades out; only releasing near the far right counts as confirmation - the whole track fills and the text becomes "Done ✓"; if released before reaching the end, the handle springs back to the start with elasticity. (GSAP Draggable type:"x", with bounds limiting it to the track, onDrag updates the filled width, onRelease checks whether it exceeds 85%; the shimmer uses background-clip:text with a moving gradient)
style_en: Slide Confirm Unlock Payment Drag Slide To Unlock Confirm Swipe Button Payment Button

desc_en: Holding it down slowly fills the progress, releasing rolls it back, and only a full fill executes it, suitable for dangerous actions like deletion
prompt_en: A button for dangerous actions (such as deletion): an outline style; when the user holds it down, a fill layer fills the whole button from left to right at a constant speed over about 1.2 seconds, and the button shrinks slightly; if released midway, the fill quickly rolls back and nothing is executed; once fully filled, the button gives a slight bounce and the text becomes "Deleted ✓". This prevents accidental taps. (CSS: the fill layer has transform:scaleX(0); while held, a class changes it to scaleX(1) with a 1.2s linear transition; on release the class is removed and it rolls back with a shorter transition; JS starts a 1.2-second timer on pointerdown and cancels it on pointerup / pointerleave)
style_en: Long Press Hold Confirm Delete Dangerous Action Progress Hold To Confirm Long Press Delete Destructive Button

desc_en: On hover, the arrow on the right slides out to the right while a new arrow slides in from the left, and the text makes way
prompt_en: A capsule button with a right-pointing arrow to the right of the text; when the mouse hovers, the right arrow slides out of the button to the right and fades out, while another identical arrow slides in from outside the left of the button to the left of the text, and the text shifts right in sync to make way, like an arrow relay pushing forward; when the mouse leaves, it reverses back. About 0.4 seconds, ease-in-out. (CSS: the button has overflow:hidden; the two arrows and the text each have transform and transition settings, switching displacement on hover)
style_en: Arrow Icon Slide In Slide Out Relay Icon Slide Arrow Button Hover CTA Button

desc_en: The border and glow brighten and dim like breathing; on hover it fills and glows strongly
prompt_en: A neon-style button: the thin border and text use an accent color, surrounded by a ring of soft outer glow and inner glow, with the halo brightening and dimming like breathing on a cycle of about 2.4 seconds; when the mouse hovers, the whole button fills, the text inverts to white, and it emits multiple layers of strong, wide-range glow. (CSS: multiple layers of box-shadow (including inset) create the glow, and keyframes change the halo size and opacity; on hover, the breathing animation stops and changes to a larger multi-layer box-shadow, with a 0.35 second transition)
style_en: Neon Glow Halo Breathing Neon Glow Pulse Button Cyberpunk Button

desc_en: After pressing copy, the icon rotates into a checkmark, and a small "Copied" hint pops up above
prompt_en: A copy button beside a line of code (or text): when pressed, the copy icon rotates, shrinks and disappears, a check icon appears with an elastic scale-up, and the button background becomes the accent color; at the same time a small "Copied" hint box pops up above the button, and after about 1.5 seconds everything returns to its original state. (CSS: the two SVG icons are stacked in the same cell, using a class to switch transform and opacity, with a transition using a bouncy cubic-bezier(.3,1.5,.5,1); the hint box is absolutely positioned above the button; JS calls navigator.clipboard.writeText, then adds the class and removes it with setTimeout)
style_en: Copy Clipboard Check Hint tooltip Feedback Copy To Clipboard Feedback Check Code Button

desc_en: Usually only a round "+" icon; on hover it expands to the right to reveal text, and the plus rotates
prompt_en: A floating action button that is usually a circle with only a "+"; when the mouse hovers, the button smoothly expands to the right into a capsule shape, revealing a text label (for example "New Project"), while the plus rotates 90 degrees at the same time; the text fades in only after the expansion is halfway; when the mouse leaves, it retracts into a circle. About 0.5 seconds. (CSS: the button has overflow:hidden, using max-width to transition from the circle's width to a larger value, the text opacity is paired with a transition-delay; the plus uses rotate(90deg))
style_en: Expand Floating Button FAB Plus Icon Button Expanding Icon Button Floating Action Reveal Label Button

desc_en: Press send, and the paper plane flies away from the button; the text changes to "Sent" and then recovers
prompt_en: A send button with a paper plane icon on its left: when pressed, the button first gives a light press and rebound, the text fades out to the right, and the paper plane first pulls back to build momentum, then accelerates up and to the right, flying out of the button and disappearing; next the text changes to "Sent" and slides in from the left; after about 1 second the text changes back to the original content, and the paper plane flies back to its original position from the lower left. (GSAP timeline: button scale 0.94 to 1, text x and opacity, the paper plane uses keyframes going up and to the right on x/y/rotation accelerating with power2.in, then add() switches the text content; the button's overflow:hidden clips the plane as it flies out)
style_en: Send Paper Plane Send Out Message Form Success Send Paper Plane Submit Button Success Button

desc_en: When checked, the box gives a bounce, the checkmark is drawn as if with a pen, and the item text gets a strikethrough
prompt_en: A checkbox for a to-do list: when clicked to check it, the box first shrinks and then bounces slightly larger (about 0.4 seconds), and its background fills; the checkmark inside is drawn from bottom-left to top-right as if with a pen; the item text on the right fades and gains a strikethrough line. When unchecked, it reverses back. (CSS: hide the native checkbox and customize the box and an SVG checkmark; the checkmark path uses stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset going from full length to 0; :checked plus style switching; the box bounces with a scale keyframes; keep a :focus-visible outline for keyboard users)
style_en: Checkbox Checkbox Check To-Do List todo Checkbox Check Animation Todo List Form Control
txt_en: Buy Coffee Beans Reply to Emails Tidy Desk

desc_en: A row of options has a slider block underneath; clicking one slides it over with a slight elasticity and changes its width
prompt_en: A capsule-shaped segmented control, for example "Day / Week / Month / Year"; beneath the current option is a solid slider block; when another option is clicked, the slider slides to the new position with a slight rebound and changes its width at the same time to fit the new option's text length; the selected text becomes a color that contrasts with the slider. About 0.45 seconds. (CSS: the slider is absolutely positioned; JS reads the clicked button's offsetLeft and offsetWidth into CSS variables, and transform:translateX(var(--x)) and width transition with cubic-bezier(.5,1.5,.5,1))
style_en: Segmented Control Switch Tabs tabs Slider Segmented Control Tabs Pill Switcher iOS Form Control

desc_en: While typing a password, the strength bar below grows segment by segment, changing with strength and showing a hint
prompt_en: Below a password input field are four strength segments: as the user types, the strength is calculated in real time (whether the length reaches 8 characters, and whether it has uppercase letters, numbers and symbols); the more conditions met, the more segments grow out from left to right; the higher the strength, the stronger the segments' visual, and the text below shows in sequence "Too Weak / Fair / Good / Very Strong"; on the right of the input is an eye button to show/hide the password; when the input is focused its border lights up. (JS: the input event calculates a score of 0-4, sets data-level and each segment's class; newly lit segments grow with a scaleX 0 to 1 keyframes)
style_en: Password Strength Signup Validation Form Password Strength Meter Signup Validation Form Control

desc_en: While dragging the slider, a value bubble pops up above, moves with the handle, and shrinks back on release
prompt_en: A range slider: the portion of the track already dragged over is filled; when the handle is held or dragged, it enlarges slightly, and a value bubble with a small triangle pops up directly above it; the bubble moves horizontally with the handle and displays the number in real time; on release the bubble shrinks and fades out. (CSS: customize the track of input[type=range] and its ::-webkit-slider-thumb; the track fill uses a background linear-gradient with a CSS variable percentage; the bubble is an absolutely positioned output, with left = handle width / 2 + (track width - handle width) x percentage, popping with scale and opacity)
style_en: Slider Lever Value Bubble Range Volume Range Slider Tooltip Bubble Value Input Form Control

desc_en: A four-box verification code; typing one box auto-advances to the next; the boxes jump up in sequence when correct, and the whole row shakes when wrong
prompt_en: A four-box verification code input: each box can hold only one digit; after typing, that box gives a light bounce and focus automatically advances to the next box; pressing Backspace in an empty box returns to the previous box and clears it; once all four boxes are filled it automatically verifies: when correct, each box jumps up in sequence and its background fills; when wrong, the whole row shakes left and right and the border changes to a warning style. (JS: each box has maxLength=1 and inputMode="numeric"; the input event focuses the next box, keydown Backspace handles going back; the result triggers CSS keyframes with a class, staggering the jumps with animation-delay; on mobile the font size is at least 16px to avoid auto-zoom)
style_en: Verification Code OTP One-Time Password SMS Login PIN Code Input Verification Auto Focus Form Control

desc_en: Usually only a round magnifier button; clicking it expands it to the left into a search box
prompt_en: Search in a navigation bar: usually just a round magnifier button; when clicked, the button smoothly expands to the left into a long search box (about 0.5 seconds), the text inside the input fades in only after the expansion is halfway, the magnifier rotates 90 degrees and a ring border lights up around it; when the input loses focus and has no content, it retracts back into a round button. (CSS: the container has overflow:hidden, width transitions from the round button's width to the expanded width with cubic-bezier(.6,0,.2,1); the input opacity is paired with a transition-delay; JS toggles the class and focuses the input)
style_en: Search Magnifier Expand Collapse Navigation Bar Expanding Search Bar Icon Input Header Form Control

desc_en: When a dropdown is opened, the panel pops out from the top, options slide in one after another, and the arrow flips
prompt_en: Dropdown menu: when the menu button is clicked, the arrow on the right flips 180 degrees, and the options panel below expands from its top edge with a slight bounce (scaleY 0.6 → 1, fading in), with the options inside sliding down and fading in one after another (each spaced about 0.05 seconds apart); when hovering over an option, its background lights up faintly; after a selection, the panel collapses and the button displays the selected value. (CSS: panel transform-origin: top, transition using cubic-bezier(.3,1.3,.5,1); each option sets --i, and on expansion transition-delay: calc(var(--i) × 0.05s))
style_en: Dropdown Menu Expand Options Sequential Dropdown Select Menu Stagger Reveal Form Control

desc_en: Type text and press Enter to turn it into a popping tag; press × or Backspace and the tag shrinks away
prompt_en: Tag input field: after the user types text and presses Enter (or a comma), the text becomes a capsule tag, enlarging from 0 with a bounce to appear in front of the input cursor; each tag has a × button on its right side, and when clicked — or when Backspace is pressed in an empty input — the last tag shrinks and fades out and the content behind it smoothly moves up to fill the gap; when the whole field is focused, its border lights up. (JS: keydown handles Enter / comma / Backspace, new elements are inserted before the input; CSS keyframes: entrance scale 0→1 using cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1), exit scale→0 using a negative margin-right to collapse, and the element is removed after animationend)
style_en: Tag tag chip Input Keywords Interests Tag Input Chips Token Field Form Control

desc_en: When switching radio options, the selected dot stretches into a droplet, slides to the new option, then bounces back into a circle
prompt_en: A set of vertically arranged radio options, where the selected dot is a separate solid small circle: when switching options, the small circle is first stretched into a vertically elongated droplet shape, slides in a straight line to the center of the new option's circle, and on arrival recovers into a circle with an elastic wobble, flowing over like a liquid; the selected outer ring changes style at the same time. (GSAP timeline: first scaleY 2.2 / scaleX 0.7, while tweening y to the new position with power3.inOut, finally scaleX/scaleY back to 1 using elastic.out(1.2,0.5); the native radio is hidden but keyboard operation is retained)
style_en: Radio radio Options Droplet Liquid Stretch Liquid Radio Button Gooey Morph Form Control
txt_en: Standard Shipping Express Delivery Store Pickup

desc_en: When a file is dragged into the area, the border lights up and the icon floats up; after dropping, a file row appears and a checkmark pops in once the progress bar finishes
prompt_en: File drag-and-drop upload area: in the middle of a dashed border there is an upload icon and “Drag files here”; when a file is dragged over the area, the border becomes solid, the background lights up faintly, and the icon floats upward; after dropping, the area bounces lightly, a file information row (file name + progress bar) pops in from below at the bottom, the progress bar fills in about 1.3 seconds, a checkmark icon pops in on the right, and after staying for one second the file row moves up and fades out. Clicking the area also lets you select files. (JS: dragenter/dragover add a class, drop reads the file name; GSAP timeline chains the bounce, the file row entrance, the progress bar scaleX 0→1, and the checkmark with back.out)
style_en: Upload File Drag-and-Drop Dragging Progress Bar Drag Drop File Upload Dropzone Progress Form Control

desc_en: A circular cursor that enlarges when passing over text, with colors inverting where it overlaps
prompt_en: The cursor is replaced with a solid circle that follows the mouse with a smooth delay; the circle uses the “difference” blend mode, and when it overlaps the text below, the colors of the text and background invert each other; when the cursor moves onto a large heading, the circle smoothly enlarges about three times so the inverted area covers more text, and shrinks back after leaving the heading. (CSS: the circle element has mix-blend-mode: difference, pointer-events: none; JS lerps toward the mouse coordinates every frame and detects whether it is within a heading's range to interpolate the scale; the container uses cursor: none to hide the native cursor)
style_en: Inverted Colors Inversion Blend Mode difference Cursor Circle Blend Mode Invert Cursor Hero Cursor Mouse

desc_en: When the cursor approaches a button it is attracted to it, deforms to wrap the whole button, and the button is also pulled slightly
prompt_en: A row of buttons in a navigation bar, with the cursor as a small circle: when the cursor approaches a button, the small circle is “sucked” over, deforms into a rounded rectangle that wraps the whole button, and its position still shifts slightly with the mouse inside the button; the button itself is also pulled slightly toward the mouse direction, and its text and background colors invert; when moving away from the button, the small circle shrinks back and the button bounces back to its original position. (GSAP: mousemove determines whether the cursor is within a button's range (with a little expansion), and if inside, tweens the cursor's x/y/width/height to the button's center and size + offset × 0.12, otherwise tweens back to a small circle; the button's x/y = offset × 0.15, power3.out)
style_en: Sticky Attraction Magnetic Deformation Wrap Navigation Sticky Cursor Magnetic Morph Nav Cursor Mouse

desc_en: A circular cursor stretches along its direction according to movement speed, and returns to a circle when it stops
prompt_en: A circular cursor follows the mouse with a smooth delay, calculating movement speed every frame: the faster it moves, the more the circle is stretched along the movement direction and flattened vertically, like elastic jelly; when the mouse stops, it slowly recovers into a perfect circle.
