(CSS: use a font that supports variable font weight, split each character into its own element, share one keyframes that varies font-weight between 100 ↔ 900, with animation-delay increasing by index)
style_en: Font Weight Thickness Variable Font Wave Breathing Variable Font Weight Wave Breathing Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: The cursor is like a lamp, and the text's long shadow always extends in the direction opposite the cursor
prompt_en: There is a large heading in a section, and the cursor position is a small glowing light source: behind the text is a long shadow made of multiple shadow layers, and the shadow always extends in the direction "away from the cursor", with layers farther away becoming fainter in color; as the cursor moves, the shadow's direction turns in real time to follow, as if the light source is moving around the text. (JS: on mousemove, compute the direction vector of the cursor relative to the text's center, and generate 18 layers of text-shadow, each layer's offset = direction × layer number, with the color gradually fading by layer number)
style_en: Light Source Projection Shadow Long Shadow 3D Cursor Light Source Long Shadow Cursor 3D Text Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: A landscape image fills the inside of large text, and the image slowly pans and zooms inside the letters
prompt_en: An extra-large, extra-bold English heading whose letters are filled with a landscape photo (the image is not visible anywhere outside the letters); the photo slowly pans and enlarges slightly inside the letters, going back and forth about once every 9 seconds, like looking at scenery through a text-shaped window; there is a very faint thin outline around the outer edges of the letters. (CSS: color:transparent + background-image + background-clip:text, with keyframes changing background-position and background-size)
style_en: Image Text Fill Knockout Background Text Mask Image Text Background Clip Knockout Mask Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: Each character in turn becomes clear and settles into place from a blurred, slightly larger state
prompt_en: Each character of a heading in turn changes from a "blurred, transparent, slightly larger, slightly lower" state to become clear and settle into position, with about 0.07 seconds between each character, giving an overall soft, refined feel; after lingering for a while, they blur out in sequence and replay. (GSAP + SplitText: fromTo on the characters {opacity:0, filter:"blur(10px)", y:".25em", scale:1.15} → {opacity:1, filter:"blur(0px)", y:0, scale:1}, ease power2.out, stagger 0.07)
style_en: Blur Emergence Letter by Letter Soft Entrance Blur In Letters Soft Reveal Stagger Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: A word is struck through with one stroke, and a new word is written out above it in handwriting, one character at a time
prompt_en: A word originally in the copy (for example "cheap") is first struck through from left to right by a slightly slanted thick line, and the original word fades; then below it, a new word (for example "affordable") pops out one character at a time in a handwritten-style font in the accent color, as if someone is revising the copy by hand, to emphasize the better wording. (GSAP timeline: the strikethrough element scaleX 0 → 1, transform-origin:left; the original word's opacity drops to 0.4; the new word is split into characters with SplitText and pops out in sequence from below with back.out)
style_en: Strike Through Strikethrough Rewrite Correction Handwriting Copy Strikethrough Rewrite Correction Copywriting Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: The other person first shows the three "typing" dots, which then turn into a message, and then your reply pops out
prompt_en: Simulate a chat interface: the other person's chat bubble first appears on the left, containing three dots bouncing up and down in sequence (typing…); after about 1.4 seconds the bubble turns into a message (for example "Are you there? I have a question~") and bounces lightly; then your reply bubble pops out on the right in the accent color (appearing by enlarging from the bottom-right corner); after lingering, they move up and fade out together, then start again. (GSAP timeline: bubbles scale 0 → 1, transform-origin set at the corner of the bubble's tail, ease back.out; the three dots use CSS keyframes with staggered animation-delay)
style_en: Chat Message Chat Box Bubble Typing Typing Indicator Customer Service Chat Bubble Typing Indicator Message Pop Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: Several hollow copies are stacked behind the text, unfolding diagonally backward in sequence, then drawing back in
prompt_en: A bold large heading, behind which 5 layers of hollow outlined copies of the same text are stacked, each layer's outline fainter the farther back it goes; during the animation these copy layers unfold in sequence (each layer delayed by about 0.06 seconds) diagonally up and to the right, forming an afterimage like an echo or a 3D staircase, linger for a moment, then draw back in to overlap the original text, looping back and forth. (CSS: multiple spans stacked in the same grid cell, using the CSS variable --i to compute the translate distance, outline opacity and animation-delay; -webkit-text-stroke creates the hollow text)
style_en: Afterimage Stacking Copies Hollow 3D Echo Echo Stack Outline Layers Repeat Text Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: "Hello" in different languages takes turns appearing, blurring in and out, while the frame's width smoothly follows along
prompt_en: At the Hero heading position, "hello" in different languages is shown in rotation (Hello, Ni Hao, Konnichiwa, Bonjour, Hola, Annyeonghaseyo, Ciao), switching about every 1.6 seconds: the old word blurs and fades out upward, and the new word blurs in from below and becomes clear; because each word has a different length, the width of the container wrapping the text smoothly scales to the new word's width, so the small dot following behind it also moves smoothly instead of jumping instantly. (GSAP: first measure the new word's width (with a hidden measuring element), tween the container's width to the new width with power3.inOut; fade the text out and in with opacity, filter:blur and y)
style_en: Multilingual Greeting Hello Hello Switching International Multilingual Greeting Hello Languages Rotate Text Heading Animated Text

desc_en: Drag a row up or down, the other rows automatically make way, and on release it springs back into place and the numbering updates
prompt_en: A list that can be reordered by dragging, each row with a drag handle on the left and a sequence number on the right: when you press and hold a row it enlarges slightly and lifts up (deeper shadow and outline), and can be dragged up and down; as you drag past the positions of other rows, the rows you pass smoothly move up or down to make way; on release, the dragged row lands in its new position with a bit of elasticity, and all the numbers update to the new order. (GSAP Draggable type:"y": while dragging, compute the target index from y ÷ row height, change the array order and tween the other rows to index × row height; on release, align with back.out)
style_en: Drag Sorting Reorder List To-do sortable Drag Reorder List Sortable Cards Group

desc_en: When you click a card to select it, an outline and a checkmark appear, and an action bar reading "N selected" pops up at the bottom
prompt_en: A row of multi-selectable image cards: when you click a card, an accent-colored outline appears around the card and it shrinks slightly, the image enlarges slightly inside the frame, and the circular checkbox in the top-right corner fills in and draws a checkmark (with a bounce-back); as long as anything is selected, a capsule-shaped action bar pops up from the bottom of the screen, showing "N selected" (the number rolls up and down when it changes) and a "Next →" button; when everything is deselected, the action bar slides back and hides. (JS toggles aria-pressed, CSS changes the outline, scale and the checkmark's stroke-dashoffset based on [aria-pressed=true]; the action bar uses translateY and opacity transitions)
style_en: Select Multi-select Check Cards Action Bar Selectable Cards Multi Select Checkbox Action Bar Cards Group

desc_en: As the cursor moves among a group of cards, the borders and interiors of the cards near it are lit up by a pool of light
prompt_en: A set of cards in a feature-introduction section arranged in a grid, each card's border a fine ring: as the cursor moves within the whole section, each card draws a soft pool of light at "the cursor's position relative to itself", so the borders of cards close to the cursor are lit up in the accent color and their interiors also carry a faint glow, while cards farther away barely light up at all; as the cursor moves between cards, the light naturally crosses the borders of neighboring cards. (CSS: the card's outer layer uses 1px of padding as the border, with background radial-gradient(circle at var(--x) var(--y), accent color, transparent); the inner layer uses another, fainter radial-gradient; on mousemove over the container, JS computes the relative coordinates for each card and writes them into --x and --y)
style_en: Border Spotlight Glow Grid Feature Introduction SaaS Linear Border Spotlight Glow Grid Feature Cards Cards Group
txt_en: Speed Security Collaboration Integration Analytics Support

desc_en: Cards form a ring and slowly rotate in 3D space, and can be dragged left and right with the mouse to spin them
prompt_en: Eight image cards form a ring in 3D space, and the whole ring slowly rotates on its own at about 24 seconds per revolution; cards at the front are larger and nearer, cards at the back are smaller and farther, and cards facing away from the viewer are hidden; the user can press and drag left and right to rotate the ring, and on release it continues rotating on its own from the current angle. (CSS 3D: perspective on the container, transform-style:preserve-3d on the ring, each card rotateY(i × 360/N) translateZ(radius), backface-visibility:hidden; GSAP loops the ring's rotationY, and Draggable pauses it while dragging and sets the angle from the displacement)
style_en: 3D Ring Carousel Carousel Ring Ring Carousel 3D Rotate Gallery Drag Cards Group
txt_en: Seaside Mountains Night Sky Afternoon City Forest Lakeside Desert

desc_en: Click two cards to flip them over; if they match they stay and bounce, if not they flip back
prompt_en: A 4 × 2 card-flipping memory mini-game: all the cards start face down, and clicking one flips it in 3D to show the pattern on its front; after two cards are flipped, if the patterns are the same, both stay face up, their background turns into the accent color and they bounce; if they differ, after lingering about 0.8 seconds both flip back face down together; text below shows the matching progress, and after all pairs are matched successfully it shows celebratory text, shuffles and starts again. (CSS: cards use transform-style:preserve-3d, front and back faces use backface-visibility:hidden, and .on applies rotateY(180deg); JS manages the flipped cards and the match checking)
style_en: Card Flip Matching Memory Game Mini-game Interactive Memory Match Card Game Flip Pairs Cards Group

desc_en: Three stat cards float up in sequence, the numbers count up, a mini line chart draws itself, and the growth rates fade in
prompt_en: Three stat cards on an admin dashboard (revenue, orders, conversion rate): on entry they float up and fade in from below in sequence (about 0.12 seconds apart), the large number in each card counts up from 0 to its target value (including thousands separators and decimals), the mini line chart below draws itself from left to right, and finally the growth percentage fades in from the left. (GSAP timeline: cards from y:30, opacity:0, with stagger; numbers use an object tween + onUpdate formatting; the line chart's polyline uses DrawSVG 0% → 100% (or stroke-dashoffset))
style_en: Dashboard Data Statistics KPI Line Chart sparkline Admin Dashboard Stat Cards KPI Sparkline Count Up Cards Group

desc_en: Click a page and it flips in 3D to the left around the spine as its axis; after flipping through them all, they flip back together to the first page
prompt_en: Like a book: on the right is a stack of pages, each page's front has an image and a page number; when clicked, the topmost page flips to the left in 3D space around the spine on its left side as its axis (about 0.9 seconds, ease-in-out), and halfway through the flip you can see the page's 3D angle; after flipping over, it shows that page's back; after flipping through them page by page, all the pages quickly flip back in sequence to the first page. (CSS 3D: each page uses transform-origin:left, transform-style:preserve-3d, front and back faces use backface-visibility:hidden, and the back uses rotateY(180deg); GSAP tweens rotationY 0 → −180, and adjusts the z-index during the flip so flipped pages stack on top)
style_en: Page Flip Book Pages Magazine Catalog E-book Page Flip Book Magazine Catalog 3D Cards Group

desc_en: A scattered stack of photos smoothly arranges into a tidy grid with one click, and stacks back up with another click
prompt_en: A scattered stack of photos (each with a wide border, randomly tilted at different angles, stacked in the center): when clicked, the photos fly one after another (about 0.04 seconds apart) smoothly into a tidy 3 × 2 grid position and straighten up; click again and they fly from the grid back into a scattered stack. About 0.7 seconds, ease-in-out. (GSAP Flip: Flip.getState(photos) → switch the container's class (from absolutely-positioned stacking to a grid layout, rotate reset to zero) → Flip.from(state, {absolute:true, stagger:.04}))
style_en: Photos Stack Spread Out Grid Album Organize Photo Pile Stack To Grid Spread Flip Cards Group

desc_en: Like a physical card, the cover opens in 3D around its left edge as its axis, revealing the image and text inside
prompt_en: A folded invitation card: at first you only see the cover (accent-colored background, a large heading and "Click to open"); when clicked, the cover flips open 180 degrees to the left in 3D space around its left side as its axis (about 0.9 seconds); the back of the cover is an image, and the right side reveals the invitation text and date on the card's inner page; at the same time the whole card shifts to the right so the opened whole stays centered; click again to close it. (CSS 3D: perspective on the container; the cover uses transform-origin:left, preserve-3d, front and back faces use backface-visibility:hidden, and the back uses rotateY(180deg); a GSAP timeline simultaneously tweens the cover's rotationY 0 → −180 and the card's xPercent 0 → 50, toggling play / reverse)
style_en: Card Folded Invitation Card Greeting Card Open 3D Folding Greeting Invitation Card Open Cards Group

desc_en: When changing pages, a thin line at the top of the page quickly runs halfway, crawls slowly, then rushes to the end and disappears once loaded, and the content then emerges in sequence
prompt_en: When the site changes pages or loads content, a thin accent-colored progress bar (with a slight glow) appears at the very top of the page: it first quickly runs to about 30%, then slowly crawls to about 70% (giving the feeling of "loading"), and when loading completes it quickly rushes to 100% and fades out; at the same time the page content (heading, paragraphs, cards) fades in and floats up in sequence from below. (GSAP timeline: the progress bar uses transform-origin:left, scaleX 0 → .3 (power2.out) → .7 (slower) → 1 (fast), then opacity 0; the content fades in with stagger)
style_en: Loading Progress Bar Top Page Change NProgress YouTube Loading Bar Page Load Progress Layout Page

desc_en: Step dots above a multi-step form: completed ones get a checkmark, the current step enlarges, and the connecting line fills along with it
prompt_en: A step indicator above a multi-step form (for example sign-up or checkout): a row of circular step numbers connected by a line; the dots of completed steps fill in and a checkmark appears with a bounce-back, the current step's outer ring lights up and it enlarges slightly, and steps not yet reached stay faint; the filled length of the connecting line smoothly extends along with the steps; below there are "Previous / Next" buttons. (CSS: the connecting line's inner layer uses transform:scaleX(current index / (total − 1)), transition 0.5 seconds; steps switch styles with .done / .on classes, and the checkmark uses keyframes from scale 0 → 1)
style_en: Steps Progress Multi-step Form Checkout Wizard Stepper Multi Step Form Wizard Progress Checkout Layout Page

desc_en: When you hover over a navigation bar item, a large multi-column menu expands below it, and each column slides in in sequence
prompt_en: A website navigation bar: when the mouse moves over "Products", a large, wide menu panel expands below it (sliding down from slightly higher up and fading in); inside, the panel is divided into three columns: two columns are link lists with small icons, and one column is a featured image card; the three columns slide up and in in sequence (about 0.06 seconds apart); when the mouse leaves the navigation area, the panel collapses. (CSS: by default the panel has opacity 0, translateY(−8px), pointer-events:none, restored when the parent has :hover or .open; each column is given a transition-delay to create the sequential appearance)
style_en: Mega Menu Dropdown Navigation Bar Multi-column mega menu Dropdown Navigation Header Layout Page
txt_en: Brand Design Web Development Motion Video Social Media Case Studies Design Guide

desc_en: Click a list item and the new page pushes in from the right while the old page retreats to the left and darkens; pressing back reverses it
prompt_en: Simulate an app's page-stack navigation: when you click an item in the list, the detail page pushes in as a full page from the right (with a shadow on its left side), while the original list page simultaneously moves about 30% to the left and darkens, as if covered over by the new page; clicking "‹ Back" in the top-left reverses it: the detail page exits to the right, and the list page moves back into place and regains its brightness. About 0.5 seconds, ease-in-out. (GSAP: the new page xPercent 100 → 0, the old page xPercent 0 → −30 with filter: brightness(.6); the reverse when going back)
style_en: Push In Page Change Back Navigation iOS Stack Push Pop Navigation Stack Page Transition App Layout Page

desc_en: When there are no search results, an empty box bounces down, its lid flips open and a question mark pops out, and the text and button appear in sequence
prompt_en: An empty state for when a search has no results or a list is empty: a simple box illustration drops from above and bounces to a stop, then the box's lid flips open around one corner as its axis, and a question mark emerges from inside and floats gently up and down; the heading, description text and "Browse all" button below fade in and move up in sequence; afterwards the lid closes and the question mark disappears. It keeps the blank screen from feeling cold and guides the next step. (GSAP timeline: the illustration from y:-20 with ease bounce.out → the lid rotation −28 with back.out → the question mark from scale 0 → the text fades in with stagger → the question mark floats with yoyo)
style_en: Empty State No Results Not Found 404 Illustration Empty State No Results Illustration Layout Page

desc_en: A cookie consent card pops up at the bottom, the cookie icon wiggles; after pressing a button it shrinks back and slides away
prompt_en: A cookie consent card at the bottom of the website: when entering the page, the card slides up from below with a bounce-back, and the cookie icon on the left elastically straightens and enlarges from a small, tilted state; inside the card there is a heading, a brief description and two buttons (Essential only / Accept all); when either button is pressed, the button presses down lightly, and the card then slides down and out and fades away. (GSAP: the card fromTo yPercent 140 → 0, ease back.out(1.4); the icon rotation −40 → 0, scale .4 → 1, ease elastic.out; on close, yPercent → 140, power3.in)
style_en: Cookie Consent Banner Privacy GDPR Notice Consent Banner Privacy Notice Layout Page

desc_en: When the "+" button in the bottom-right corner is clicked it turns into a "×", and several small action buttons and labels pop out above it in sequence
prompt_en: A circular floating action button (+) in the bottom-right corner of the screen: when clicked, the button rotates 135 degrees into a ×, a translucent overlay covers the background, and three small circular action buttons pop out above it from bottom to top in sequence, each with a text label on its left (for example New note, Take a photo, Share a link), appearing by enlarging with a bounce-back from a smaller, slightly lower position; click again or click the overlay to retract them in the reverse order. (CSS: when .open, the main button uses rotate(135deg); each action item is given a --i, transitions transform: translateY + scale, with transition-delay computed by index, in the reverse order when collapsing)
style_en: Floating Button FAB Expand Quick Actions Speed Dial Floating Action Button Menu Layout Page

desc_en: When you scroll to the bottom, a spinning "loading more" appears, and new content then floats up one item after another
prompt_en: Infinite scrolling on a social feed wall or article list: when the user scrolls to the bottom of the list, a spinning loading indicator and "Loading more…" appear at the bottom; after about a second, a new batch of cards is appended after the list, fading in and floating up from below in sequence (about 0.12 seconds apart), and the user can keep scrolling down. (Implementation: use IntersectionObserver to watch a sentinel element at the bottom of the list; when it enters the viewport, show the loading indicator and request the next page; after the new cards are inserted, use GSAP from y:24, opacity:0, with stagger for the entrance)
style_en: Infinite Scroll Load More Pagination Feed Wall Infinite Scroll Load More Feed Pagination Layout Page

desc_en: Click to collapse an admin sidebar to just icons, the text fades out, and the main content area widens in sync
prompt_en: The sidebar on the left of an admin interface: when you click the collapse button at the top of the sidebar, the sidebar's width smoothly narrows to fit only the icons (about 0.45 seconds), the text of each item simultaneously fades out to the left, and the main content area on the right widens in sync; click again to expand and the text fades back in; the currently active item has a faint accent background color. (CSS: the sidebar uses a width transition, cubic-bezier(.6,0,.2,1); item text transitions opacity and translateX, with white-space:nowrap + overflow:hidden to prevent wrapping; the main content uses flex:1 to fill automatically)
style_en: Sidebar Collapse Expand Admin Dashboard Collapsible Sidebar Nav Dashboard Admin Layout Page

desc_en: Press ⌘K and a search panel pops up; as you type it filters the commands, the selected item lights up, and pressing Enter runs it
prompt_en: A command palette like ⌘K: when the shortcut is pressed, the background blurs and darkens, and a search panel pops up at the top center of the screen (appearing by enlarging from a slightly smaller, slightly higher position); the input field has a blinking cursor, and all the commands are listed below; as the user types, the list filters in real time to keep only the matching items, and the first matching item lights up with an accent background color and shows a ↵ hint; pressing Enter makes that item flash once and closes the panel. (JS: a keydown listener for Meta/Ctrl + K opens it; an input event filters the list; CSS transitions the panel from opacity + scale(.95) → 1, and the background uses backdrop-filter:blur)
style_en: Command Palette Shortcut Search Cmd K Command Palette Spotlight Quick Search Layout Page

desc_en: Map pins drop down in sequence on a map, a route is drawn from the start point to the end point, and a small dot advances along the route
prompt_en: A simplified map background (faint landmass outlines and latitude/longitude grid lines), on which three map pins drop down from above in sequence and bounce to a stop, each labeled with a place name below it; then a route is drawn from the start point along a curved path all the way to the end point (about 2.2 seconds), while a small dot with a halo advances along the route; on reaching the end point, the end-point pin bounces once. (GSAP: the pins from y:-30 + bounce.out with stagger; the route uses DrawSVG 0% → 100%; the small dot uses MotionPathPlugin to move along the same path, with a duration matching the line drawing; beneath it there is also a faint dashed line indicating the full route)
style_en: Map Route Navigation Pin Location Journey Delivery Logistics Map Route Path Pin Delivery Journey Graphics SVG

desc_en: An analog clock showing the current time, whose second hand ticks one mark each second with a slight bounce-back
prompt_en: An analog clock showing the actual current time: the dial has 60 tick marks (every 5th one thicker and longer), the hour and minute hands move continuously and smoothly, and the second hand, in the accent color, ticks one mark every second, slightly overshooting within about 0.15 seconds as it ticks and then bouncing back into place, like a real mechanical watch. (JS requestAnimationFrame: read the hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds from Date and compute each hand's angle; second hand angle = (seconds − 1 + bounce-back curve(milliseconds/150)) × 6 degrees; SVG lines use transform rotate)
style_en: Clock Hands Second Hand Real-time Time Clock Analog Watch Time Real-time Graphics SVG

desc_en: A sunny sun slowly rotates, clouds drift, raindrops fall, and lightning flashes
prompt_en: A set of weather icon cards: in the sunny one, the sun and its rays slowly rotate on their own; in the cloudy one, the clouds drift gently left and right; in the rainy one, raindrops continuously fall from below the cloud at staggered times and fade out; in the thunderstorm one, the lightning is dim most of the time and occasionally flashes twice quickly. The weather name is labeled below each icon. (SVG + CSS keyframes: the sun rotates, one revolution in 10 seconds; the clouds move back and forth with translateX; the raindrops use translateY + opacity with staggered animation-delay; the lightning flickers using keyframes with steps(1))
style_en: Weather Icons Sun Cloud Rain Lightning icon Weather Icons Animated Sun Cloud Rain Thunder Graphics SVG

desc_en: The lines of a dashed selection box flow continuously, there are handles at its four corners, and the size figures update in real time as the box changes size
prompt_en: A selection box like those in design tools: a dashed rectangle frames the content, the dashes flow continuously in the same direction (commonly called marching ants), and there are square handles at the four corners; the selection box's size changes smoothly between two sizes, and the size label below it (width × height) updates its figures in real time along with it. (SVG rect: stroke-dasharray 6 5, with keyframes looping stroke-dashoffset from 0 to −11 infinitely; the box's width/height are changed with CSS keyframes; JS periodically reads the size and updates the label)
style_en: Selection Box Dashed Line Marching Ants Handles Design Tool Figma Marching Ants Selection Box Handles Graphics SVG

desc_en: An irregular, soft blob keeps slowly morphing, with another fainter shadow layer behind it
prompt_en: An organic, irregular blob (like soft liquid or jelly) whose edges are driven by multiple sets of sine waves at different frequencies, continuously and slowly morphing and never repeating; behind it there is also a slightly larger, fainter shadow layer in the same color morphing at a different rhythm, adding depth; text is placed in the center of the blob. (JS requestAnimationFrame: take 8 control points distributed around a circle, radius = base + the sum of several sin(time + index × phase) values, and use Catmull-Rom to convert them into a smooth cubic Bézier curve written into the path's d)
style_en: Organic Blob Spot Flowing Morphing Liquid Blob Organic Shape Morph Liquid Graphics SVG

desc_en: A hexagonal badge's outline is drawn, a star shrinks from large and stamps onto it, and rays radiate all around
prompt_en: A badge animation for when an achievement is earned: the outline of the hexagonal badge is first drawn in one stroke along its edges, then its interior fades in to fill it; a star quickly shrinks from a very large, rotating, transparent state down to the center of the badge with a bounce-back, like stamping it on; at the same time, a ring of short rays around the badge shoots rapidly outward from the inside and disappears, and the badge as a whole bounces lightly once; the achievement name and the words "Achievement unlocked" below emerge in sequence. (GSAP timeline: DrawSVG draws the outline → fillOpacity → the star fromTo scale 3 → 1, rotation −60 → 0, back.out → the rays DrawSVG "0% 0%" → "0% 100%" → "100% 100%")
style_en: Badge Achievement Unlock Reward Gamification Badge Achievement Unlock Reward Gamification Graphics SVG

desc_en: An ECG waveform is drawn from left to right, a glowing cursor dot advances along the line, and the heart-rate figure beside it pulses
prompt_en: An ECG display for a medical or health app: on a dark screen with fine grid lines, a glowing ECG waveform (flat line, small wave, the sharp QRS wave, T wave, repeating) is drawn from left to right, and a glowing cursor dot advances along with the drawing front; after drawing to the end, the line begins disappearing from the left side and is redrawn; the top-right shows a heart-rate figure (occasionally varying slightly) and a heart beating regularly. (GSAP: DrawSVG "0% 0%" → "0% 100%" to draw it out, then to "100% 100%" to make it disappear; the cursor dot uses MotionPathPlugin along the same path; the heart uses scale yoyo)
style_en: ECG Heartbeat Waveform Health Medical Monitoring ECG Heartbeat Pulse Monitor Health Graphics SVG

desc_en: The trunk grows first, then branches split off, and finally the leaves emerge one by one
prompt_en: A tree grows from the bottom up: first the ground line and the main trunk are drawn (about 0.8 seconds), then branches to the left and right grow out in sequence, followed by finer twigs; after the branches are drawn, leaves pop out one by one from the ends of the branches in random order (enlarging from 0 to 1, with a bounce-back); finally text emerges below. Suitable for brand stories, growth or sustainability themes. (GSAP timeline: each branch is an SVG path, drawn in sequence with DrawSVG 0% → 100%; the leaves use scale 0 → 1, transform-origin at the leaf stem, stagger from:"random")
style_en: Tree Growing Plant Branches Leaves Growth Sustainability Growing Tree Plant Branches Leaves Growth Graphics SVG

desc_en: Three gears of different sizes mesh together, driving each other at different speeds according to their tooth-count ratio
prompt_en: Three gears of different sizes and tooth counts mesh with each other: the largest gear rotates clockwise at a fixed speed, and the two smaller gears meshing with it rotate counterclockwise at higher speeds according to their tooth-count ratio (the one with fewer teeth turns faster), with tooth aligned to tooth and no clipping, like a mechanical system in operation; suitable for "processing", settings or system-status screens. (SVG: generate each gear's outline path programmatically from its radius and tooth count; GSAP loops each gear's rotation infinitely, with a small gear's angular velocity = the large gear × (large tooth count ÷ small tooth count), in the opposite direction, and sets the initial phase so the teeth align)
style_en: Gears Linked Mechanism Running Settings System Gears Cogs Mechanism Rotation Settings Graphics SVG

desc_en: Fingerprint ridges are drawn ring by ring, a scanning light bar sweeps up and down, and after success the frame glows and a checkmark appears
prompt_en: A phone fingerprint-unlock screen: in a rounded-square sensing area, the fingerprint's curved ridges are drawn in sequence ring by ring from the inside out; then a glowing scanning light bar sweeps from top to bottom and back from bottom to top, and the text below shows "Scanning…"; after the scan completes, the fingerprint ridges fade, a thick checkmark is quickly drawn, the sensing area's frame emits a glow, and the text changes to "Verified". (GSAP timeline: the fingerprint arcs are drawn with DrawSVG stagger; the scanning bar top 0% → 100% yoyo; on completion, add a class to make the frame's box-shadow glow, and the checkmark DrawSVG 0% → 100%)
style_en: Fingerprint Scan Unlock Biometric Verification Login Fingerprint Scan Biometric Unlock Auth Graphics SVG
